items.name: Zach (Project Manager)
items.desc: joined CC37 (January 2023) as project manager, tasked with organizing multiple parallel deliverables; by CC44 was helping flesh out individual projects, define acceptance criteria, and plan MVP delivery across teams. (CC37, CC44)

items.name: Tobias (Environment Artist)
items.desc: joined CC31 (late 2022) from Germany; trained and assigned to Solace environment art, freeing David to focus more on Esperanza. (CC31)

items.name: Julian (Project Manager)
items.desc: joined January 2022 as an IT project manager/scrum master; organized the previously scrambling team structure across UK/Europe and North America, running daily agile standups across 5-6 concurrent projects, and set up sprint organization (via Asana) across mobile, PC game, and marketing efforts. (CC3, CC9)

items.name: Greg (Node/Backend Architecture)
items.desc: after early-stage hiring talks (CC76), Greg (a veteran in network client-server and commercial development) joined to redesign node architecture for efficiency, working with Jeff and the AWS team on the node backend; architecture finalization with implementation to follow. (CC76, CC80, CC81)

items.name: Michael (React Developer)
items.desc: a React developer hire was confirmed (CC30), then started (CC33), found within the Cornucopias community; responsible for website redesign, Copious Academy, portfolio dashboard, and desktop launcher frontend, helping centralize coding across multiple parallel projects. (CC30, CC33)

items.name: Full-time animator
items.desc: hired CC42 (early 2023), the first dedicated animator on the team; completed male and female locomotion sets (walk, jog, run, idle) and moved on to climbing and other interaction animations, enabling the character animation system to progress rapidly. (CC42)

items.name: Junior Environment Artists
items.desc: an ongoing hiring thread to accelerate land/zone art production for Solace, Esperanza and Fortune: recruitment began (CC79), the first hire completed final interviews (CC81), three more joined (CC83), several more were added and trained on Unreal Engine workflows (CC85), and a plan to add four junior developers for Solace sectors (then four more for Esperanza) was set (CC39). (CC39, CC79, CC81, CC83, CC85)

items.name: Progression System Backend Hire
items.desc: a new hire joined to implement the backend architecture and progression system per existing crafting/progression planning docs (CC80); a second hire with full-stack and long Cardano development history joined to build the Achievement/progression system backend, starting with server-side holo-cache data saving (CC81). (CC80, CC81)

items.name: Team Growth Timeline
items.desc: headcount grew steadily throughout development: 18 employees in Q1 2022 up to ~27 by Q4 2022 (CC36); over 50 people including externals/mods by CC35; job security guaranteed for three years with hiring funded gradually via POA sales (CC11); two new members onboarded in Q2 with more planned for Q3/Q4 (CC57); grew to 33 people with a further 10-20% planned for 2024 (CC75); to 42 internal full-time staff / 60+ with contractors (CC83); 11 new hires in a single 90-day sprint bringing the team past 70 (CC86); 7+ new members added with more programmers sought (CC89); to 52 members (CC92); plans to grow to 40-50 by end of 2024 (CC81); continued growth funded by land grab/market sales (CC141); further staffing expansion planned for 2026 (CC147). (CC11, CC35, CC36, CC57, CC75, CC81, CC83, CC86, CC89, CC92, CC141, CC147)

items.name: Josh Jones (Social Media Manager)
items.desc: a new social media manager joined the team (CC86) and was publicly announced as Josh Jones, previously the 'Late Game Crypto' content creator (CC88). (CC86, CC88)

items.name: Process Building & Agile Methodology
items.desc: project management processes and systems were built out across marketing, art, PC game, mobile game, and desktop launcher teams to position the company to scale (CC8); Zach later spent five months implementing agile methodology across all development teams, setting up sprints, task backlogs, and cross-departmental coordination (CC54). (CC8, CC54)

items.name: Team Events
items.desc: plans confirmed for team-building events through the year, including smaller workshop-style meetups for globally distributed team members (CC11) and a US-based team retreat/workshop week in Colorado (CC12). (CC11, CC12)

items.name: Discord Moderator Program
items.desc: a weekly meeting with moderators was implemented to improve communication after mods felt out of the loop (CC24), followed by a moderator training program to bolster the Discord moderation crew (CC25). (CC24, CC25)

items.name: Founder/Employee Token Vesting
items.desc: founders agreed to double their token vesting period (same start date, halved distribution pace), with nearly full team agreement (CC31); the employee token release schedule was later finalized after resolving tax/compliance hurdles, with many team members electing to extend their vesting. (CC31, CC45)

items.name: QA Team
items.desc: the QA department (led by Anon) tested the web interface across browsers/devices while moving from laptops to proper hardware ahead of full game testing (CC51); two new QA hires joined from the community with plans for more, supporting Solace testing passes (CC83). (CC51, CC83)

items.name: Jim (Technical Director)
items.desc: one of the co-founders; responsible for technical architecture, multiplayer systems, UE5 development, and game physics (CC1)

items.name: David (Creative Director)
items.desc: one of the co-founders; responsible for art direction, environment creation, NPC design, lore, and game visuals (CC1)

items.name: Jeff (UI/UX Director)
items.desc: responsible for UI/UX design across the game, desktop launcher, and website; involved since early development; also supports quality assurance and testing processes alongside Ant (CC1, CC48)

items.name: Mark (Designer / Video Editor)
items.desc: joined September 2021; responsible for in-game brand designs, land deck imagery, POA artwork support, UI design contributions, and Copi Cafe video editing (CC31)

items.name: Dean / Declan (Mobile Game Developer)
items.desc: lead developer on the Running Gun UE5 mobile game; moved development from Mac to Windows for better UE5 performance; to be introduced to the community with a demo when timing is right; joined the team approximately 18 months prior --- originally built the earlier Unity-based mobile game before it was shelved; moved to the UE5 team around Christmas; now leading the in-game menu build, including controller support (mouse/keyboard/controller) (CC38, CC55)

items.name: Senior DevOps / networking engineer
items.desc: hired around CC22; responsible for cloud multiplayer infrastructure, server architecture, and the replication systems underpinning multiplayer (CC22)

items.name: Junior developers (4--8 planned)
items.desc: planned hire of 4--8 junior UE5 developers in approximately 3 months from CC39 to accelerate Solace sector production; some mobile team members being redeployed to Solace following Running Gun shelving (CC39)

items.name: Monte Carlo / economy simulation consultancy
items.desc: Machinations confirmed as Monte Carlo simulation partner (CC47) --- contract signed; will model game economy, run contingency plans, test for inflation/deflation events, and pursue "Verified by Machinations" seal; full engagement later in 2023; preliminary modelling for racing game first; employee token release schedule finalised by Ben (Director of Finance) after compliance process (CC45) (CC42, CC45, CC47)

items.name: Ant (Chief Quality Officer / Co-founder)
items.desc: one of the four co-founders of Cornucopious; leads quality assurance across all game releases; oversees the racing game testing tier rollout process; described as shy but mentioned as a future Copi Cafe guest (CC46)

items.name: Machinations (economy simulation partner)
items.desc: specialist company hired to run Monte Carlo simulations on the in-game economy; translates game design documents into diagrams; simulates all possible outcomes and tests for inflation and deflation events; verifies if the game economy passes criteria for the "Verified by Machinations" seal (balanced, sustainable, and unexploitable economy); contract signed CC47; full engagement planned later in 2023; preliminary modelling for the racing game first (CC47)

items.name: Hiring More Experienced Developers
items.desc: The team has been heavily interviewing additional experienced developers (not junior-level) to bring on soon, as part of a strategy to build quickly and remain lean ahead of the next bull cycle. (CC64)

items.name: New Database/API Hire (33rd Employee)
items.desc: Cornucopias announced bringing on their 33rd permanent employee, a hire focused on database and API setup for game data transmission (XP, progression, etc.). (CC66)

items.name: New Staff Additions
items.desc: The team hired a new junior artist working on Solace/Solace 2 assets, and brought on 'Scruffy' full-time to handle testing and social media/live streaming. (CC70)

items.name: Marketing Director Role Change
items.desc: Matt moved laterally from Community/POA Director to Marketing Director just before this episode to support a ramp-up in marketing efforts. (CC79)

items.name: Team Page and Careers Page
items.desc: Team is building out a team page and careers page as part of hiring efforts to accelerate delivery this year. (CC79)

items.name: Props Artist Hiring
items.desc: The team is actively going through a number of new hires, including props artists, to speed up sector development and allow more parallel work. (CC82)

items.name: Senior Game Systems Programmer
items.desc: New senior game systems programmer hired to work on systems such as AI/NPC movement and gameplay mechanics like mining and fishing. (CC83)

items.name: UK HR Hire
items.desc: New HR person hired to manage the UK side of the growing team, complementing existing US/Europe HR coverage as the company scales. (CC83)

items.name: Marketing Director Hire (Matt Nations)
items.desc: Matt Nations brought on as Marketing Director roughly three weeks prior, tasked with building marketing processes, delegating tasks, and driving the goal of making Cornucopias a household name in web3. (CC83)

items.name: Advisory Board Expansion
items.desc: Cornucopias officially onboarded three new advisers: Philip Black (game economist, ex-Zynga/Amazon Games/EA, already helped with the published copi utility and game economy planning), Jen Donaho (marketing expert from League of Legends), and Eric Peterson (Star Citizen co-founder/Wing Commander designer). First advisory call held last week with monthly meetings planned going forward. (CC100)

items.name: Unreal Engine Developer Recruitment
items.desc: Team is actively recruiting additional Unreal Engine game programmers to speed up development of game loops, aiming to onboard one before year end and then roughly one to two per month afterward, targeting a team size around 100. Mentioned delivery timing: one hire before end of year, then 1-2/month. (CC114)

items.name: New Art Team Members
items.desc: Several new art team members were hired this year including Jillian, Katherine, Devin, and intern Antoine, helping build out Solace's environment and props. (CC115)

items.name: New Programmer Hires
items.desc: A new programmer is being brought on board within about two weeks, with plans to add 3-6 more programmers over the first six months of 2025 to scale up gameplay development. Mentioned delivery timing: Within two weeks / first 6 months of 2025. (CC116)

items.name: New Developer/Programmer Hire
items.desc: Team announced a new developer/programmer joining to help increase gameplay output. (CC118)

items.name: Video Production Team
items.desc: Team is building up a video production team to produce more marketing videos as part of scaling marketing efforts. (CC118)

items.name: Crafting Programmer Hire
items.desc: A new programmer focused specifically on crafting is joining the team in a couple of weeks to help build out the crafting system. Mentioned delivery timing: starts in a couple of weeks. (CC119)

items.name: Monthly Cross-Department Show & Tell
items.desc: Following a successful team meeting where each department (art, environment, programming, creatures) presented their in-progress work, the team confirmed plans to make this cross-department show-and-tell a recurring monthly event. Mentioned delivery timing: once a month. (CC121)

items.name: Alpha Launch Fundraising Round
items.desc: The team is actively building relationships with VC groups and an investment banker in preparation for a fundraising round timed around the alpha launch to support team growth. Mentioned delivery timing: around alpha launch time. (CC139)

items.name: Marketing team changes (Scruffy & Zeke)
items.desc: Matt is departing marketing to pursue other interests; Scruffy is stepping up and Zeke has joined as a new marketing team member focused on gathering community content. (CC157)

items.name: Internal Communications Platform Switch
items.desc: The team switched off Telegram onto a new internal communications platform this week to create more efficient communication, part of broader organizational restructuring as the team scales. (CC2)

items.name: Callum's Transition to Video Content Role
items.desc: Callum, previously handling social media scheduling, is moving into producing YouTube videos, team interviews, walkthroughs, and event footage, starting with filming the Manchester trip. (CC12)

items.name: Financial Analyst Hire
items.desc: A newly hired Certified Financial Analyst with extensive M&A, budgeting, and finance background has joined the team to help manage complex crypto financials and improve tokenomics understanding. (CC14)

items.name: Gaming Artist Hire
items.desc: An artist from the UK has joined the team to help speed up production of artwork for the game's sectors, with the first sector still months away from announcement. (CC14)

items.name: New Team Hires
items.desc: A new artist has joined the team and is quickly picking up cutting-edge processes; Steve ('Pops' from Discord) has joined full-time after multiple departments sought him out. Additional interviews are ongoing for an artist/UE5 developer and a junior apprentice role. Two new hires confirmed: a senior devops/networking engineer (promoted from an existing contractor role) to build cloud multiplayer infrastructure, and a skilled 3D animator/artist to support and expand the art team. (CC15, CC22)

items.name: New Hires: Multiplayer Network Engineer & Senior Technical Artist
items.desc: Team is actively hiring a multiplayer network engineer to improve multiplayer systems ahead of the 2023 Alpha, and a senior technical artist to support David's art team. Mentioned delivery timing: Ahead of 2023 Alpha. (CC21)

items.name: Junior Analyst for Crafting Economy
items.desc: A junior analyst has been hired to help build out the in-game crafting/processing economy (raw materials to finished products), starting the following Monday. Mentioned delivery timing: starts Monday. (CC23)

items.name: Employee Wellness & Benefits Program
items.desc: Company has launched an ADP-based benefits program in the US and is moving to implement a similar program in the UK, alongside consideration of a wellness program for staff. (CC29)

items.name: Programmer & Animator Hiring
items.desc: Team is actively interviewing more programmers and plans to add an animator and additional team members before the next major development cycle, roughly a year to a year and a half away. (CC37)

items.name: Finance Team Expansion
items.desc: Alex, a recent finance/accounting graduate, has joined under Director of Finance Ben to help track accounting, crypto wallets, and fund management. (CC55)

items.name: Solace (Zones 1, 2 & 3)
items.desc: Cornucopias' starting world region (internally 'Life on the Farm'); confirmed early and built out over roughly two years: proprietary world-building tools, water/foliage/nanite tech, weather and day/night systems, and a scavenger hunt system were developed alongside it; all three 8km x 8km domes were hand-built with curated (non-procedural) geography, QA-tested down to ~60-70 bugs, and publicly released at Rare Evo (~a month ahead of schedule); ongoing polish (tree/rock texture variety, deep forest detail, performance optimization, land plot development) continued after release. (CC1, CC9, CC10, CC22, CC23, CC24, CC25, CC35, CC36, CC37, CC39, CC45, CC48, CC50, CC53, CC56, CC57, CC58, CC61, CC63, CC64, CC69, CC70, CC71, CC72, CC75, CC76, CC78, CC81, CC83, CC84, CC86, CC87, CC88, CC91, CC92, CC93, CC94, CC95, CC99, CC100, CC101, CC102, CC111, CC115, CC126, CC142)

items.name: Esperanza (Zones 1, 2 & 3)
items.desc: the desert/canyon-themed region following Solace (internally 'Wild West'); development began in tandem with Solace, with art/asset production, a hub city mirroring Solace's, and glimpse-preview areas shown ahead of full release; as of the most recent mention the zones exist but still need polish and hub-to-hub travel work, with full release timing having slipped several times. (CC1, CC9, CC27, CC31, CC56, CC57, CC63, CC75, CC83, CC87, CC90, CC92, CC99, CC101, CC102, CC104, CC114, CC116, CC119, CC121, CC126, CC128, CC130, CC132, CC137, CC140, CC148)

items.name: Fortune (Zones 1, 2 & 3)
items.desc: the third full world region after Esperanza (internally 'Eastern,' later revealed as Japan/samurai-themed); name finalized early, with the first revealed in-world asset being a Double Dragon Mythic weapon; zone work had started as of the most recent mention but remains early-stage relative to Solace/Esperanza. (CC1, CC9, CC17, CC27, CC75, CC148)

items.name: Zone 4 (Isola)
items.desc: the fourth planned world zone, originally teased as a volcanic-island theme (Canary Islands/Greece, black sand) but ultimately decided by community vote as 'Isola,' a tropical rainforest zone (Thailand/SE Asia); confirmed to be developed only after Esperanza and Fortune are delivered, with a possible land sale later. (CC1, CC18, CC23, CC106, CC154)

items.name: Calido Valley / Resort / Megadome
items.desc: the game's starter/tutorial zone (replacing the originally planned 'Starter Island'); built out as a metaverse hub with a resort, racing pavilion, city district (financial district above, cyberpunk area below), international airport, observation tower with a quantum barrier shield reveal, a nighttime/midnight mode, and the Cornucopias Labs facility; used throughout as a controlled public-testing ground for core systems (multiplayer, compass, holo caches, voice chat) before those systems moved to Solace. (CC47, CC52, CC57, CC60, CC62, CC63, CC64, CC65, CC74, CC75, CC114, CC115, CC120, CC127, CC130, CC132)

items.name: World-building tools & production pipeline
items.desc: internal tooling built to speed up zone creation: an asset/environment tool, a grid-based work-assignment system (refined from ~100 small boxes down to ~20 larger ones, then to a 36-box 'work box' system), a land-first build order (full terrain before land plots), and supporting QA/bug-report tooling (auto system-spec capture, GPS-tagged bug reports). (CC37, CC38, CC56, CC63, CC71)

items.name: World scale & theme-zone planning
items.desc: overall plan of 12 theme zones (each with multiple 8km x 8km maps, home bubbles, and custom domes), described at full scale as 36 handcrafted domes (~26x the size of GTA 5); sectors-per-zone was later reduced from ten to five based on performance testing, with four districts per sector; three zones (Solace, Esperanza, Fortune) plus a starter island were formally announced early via the Copi Wiki. (CC1, CC32, CC36, CC44, CC49)

items.name: Hub cities & Central City
items.desc: each major zone gets its own central hub city (mirroring Solace's 'Reserve at Solace,' with apartment areas, stores, and a real-estate building); Esperanza and Fortune hubs are planned similarly, each sized for 50,000-100,000 players; medical center/respawn-point buildings were added to Solace and Kid Toledo; underground tunnel areas beneath the hub city were also revealed as an upcoming traversable feature. A separate, longer-term 'Central City' metaverse/B2B hub was also confirmed as planned but described as far off. (CC82, CC134, CC136, CC139, CC143, CC144)

items.name: The Alleian (starting ship/hub)
items.desc: a new luxury ship serving as the starting location/onboarding area for early access players (in-lore donated by a billionaire), featuring a spawn area, banners, and a globe display; replaced the previous scattered spawn points, though guide/NPC/task content was still to come as of its introduction. (CC129, CC132)

items.name: Land sale & land districts system
items.desc: moved away from the original whitepaper model (40 villages/36 houses) to a districts system where each zone contains multiple land masses/districts with different utility (mining, fishing, etc.); the first of two planned zone land sales covered fixed-supply playable land across three zones, previewed with a cave-environment teaser clip and early UE5 land-environment renders (e.g. Aspen trees). (CC3, CC4, CC6, CC7)

items.name: Cardano World
items.desc: A new custom-dome-based world showcasing the Cardano ecosystem is in development, featuring sections like DeFi, metaverse, profile POAs, and gaming, with a Cardano headquarters and teleport links to individual projects' custom domes. Cardano World is being built within the game space, intended to feature different Cardano-related projects, such as headquarters custom domes discoverable by exploring the zone. (CC14, CC15)

items.name: Prison system
items.desc: A prison area/game has been built (in development for ~6 months) for players who get bounties from griefing; includes activities to do while imprisoned and mechanics for escaping, tied into the bounty/security system already live. (CC157)

items.name: Sector Areas / Lost Bubbles
items.desc: Planned unowned 'no man's land' sector areas (called 'lost bubbles') featuring open PVP, destroyed infrastructure, underground cave sections opening to exposed landscape, and rogue AI/robots. Described as a later stage of development. (CC66)

items.name: Glimpse of Fear (formerly Glimpse of Soulless)
items.desc: The zone previously called Glimpse of Soulless has been renamed and reworked into Glimpse of Fear, tied to a new Quantum Monster story (Julia's story) coming in this build. Mentioned delivery timing: very soon. (CC109)

items.name: New Global Map & Antique Shop
items.desc: New global map area shown featuring free apartments, large skyscrapers/buildings, and a new antique shop (still uncolored/WIP) which serves as the starting point for the Relic Quest. (CC150)

items.name: Environment, Lighting & Post-Processing
items.desc: Environment asset shaders and post-processing got major updates with detail passes across assets, noticeably elevating overall visual quality in the Mythical Sunrise build; additional lumen/lighting work for Solace further enhanced contrast and visuals on 4K displays; a full day/night cycle later shipped running a complete 24-hour cycle in 4 real-world hours, consistent across all zones (Solace, Esperanza, etc.) as part of the living-world design. (CC67, CC68, CC71)

items.name: Compass
items.desc: an icon-based HUD guiding players toward nearby points of interest, tasks, fishing spots, mines, races, and mystery locations, confirmed early and explicitly kept distinct from the planned mini-map; later evolved into a fuller guidance system with icons/key helping new players find locations like Calido Raceway and public transport, built on existing tech and planned to grow into a tasking/XP system with mystery map markers. (CC1, CC72, CC105)

items.name: Mini-Map
items.desc: referenced early as a future addition to the compass HUD, explicitly kept as a separate feature from the compass itself; confirmed as coming but not being actively resourced (estimated ~6 months out), with placement (e.g. top-right overlay) still undecided since priority stayed on core systems. (CC1, CC72, CC84)

items.name: Directional Pointer
items.desc: a screen-edge-snapping indicator (up to 10 simultaneous targets) originally built for the Delivery Quest, adopted as a core quality-of-life navigation feature; later extended to show distance/text detail (e.g. floor number, drop-off instructions) for finding specific locations like apartment blocks. (CC1, CC151, CC152)

items.name: Map System
items.desc: the full pop-up/interactive map (land blocks, custom player-placed markers) confirmed early, evolving through an in-house map system with public land-plot data, a toggleable land-plot/resource overlay, high-def overhead views, a GTA-style legend (major locations, stores, ATMs), and waypoint/destination selection feeding into the compass; released as Map System v2 (filter/search, set markers, compass navigation) with further tools for locating and visualizing claimed land plots by rarity/status, and ongoing 3D map rendering work for Solace. (CC1, CC53, CC100, CC101, CC104, CC111, CC129, CC132, CC134, CC142, CC144, CC147)

items.name: Keyboard remapping
items.desc: planned for future builds (requested by community) (CC1)

items.name: Land plot scanner
items.desc: in-game scanning utility that lets players scan the world to locate and identify their land plots on the map (CC1)

items.name: New Jump Puzzles
items.desc: More jump puzzles, including a larger one called 'the monstrosity,' are being added in the Calido Magic Hour update. Mentioned delivery timing: Friday (this week). (CC65)

items.name: Day/Night Cycle Testing
items.desc: The team has been releasing builds representing different times of day (Golden Hour, Mythic Sunshine) specifically to test performance and lighting issues; performance has improved and a full day/night cycle (ranging from 8 to 24 hours) is being worked toward. Mentioned delivery timing: coming soon. (CC68)

items.name: Trail & Points of Interest System
items.desc: Trails will run throughout the different sectors/zones with special interest points along them for players to discover; trail markers are not yet active in the current build but are planned. (CC72)

items.name: Resource/Points-of-Interest Info Device & Web Map
items.desc: An in-game device (hologram/graphic) will show resources and points of interest near a land plot, mirrored on an interactive web map for the land rush where players can zoom and favorite locations. (CC85)

items.name: Wrist-Mounted Visualizer Device
items.desc: In-game wrist-mounted computer shows a holographic visualization of land plots with serial numbers and nearby resources, used for prospecting during the land rush. (CC91)

items.name: Land Detector / Scanner Device
items.desc: A new device that lets players wander the land, activate a beam to locate land blocks, and preview plot sizes (small, medium, large) ahead of the land grab. (CC100)

items.name: Land Plot Scanner
items.desc: A feature that shows POA/land-plot holders where their land plots are located within the new Solace domes, driving community excitement and heavy server load for testing. (CC101)

items.name: Land Grab Web Map & High-Res Land Plot Images
items.desc: Team is building a web-based map for the land rush showing wallet-linked land plots, filters, favorites, and eventually high-resolution 4K/8K explorable images of each plot taken in-Unreal Engine; MVP is close to release with a big update expected next week. Mentioned delivery timing: next week (update), MVP imminent. (CC114)

items.name: Land Favoriting / Interactive Land Map
items.desc: A web-based back-end map tool letting players log into their account, view the full land map across three sub-maps, favorite plots they are interested in, and take actions from the plot page; expected to add per-property photos in the future. Mentioned delivery timing: Imminent, this week or next. (CC115)

items.name: New Onboarding Flow (World Breaker to Museum)
items.desc: The game's starting sequence is being reworked so players exit the World Breaker into a new Loading Bay and then into a Museum area with lore, fixing disorientation issues from the previous build where players spawned with no context. Mentioned delivery timing: next build (553). (CC120)

items.name: Terra Tunnel
items.desc: A new Terra tunnel has been built as part of the content coming in the next build. (CC128)

items.name: New Parking Area
items.desc: A new parking area has been built out as part of the upcoming build's content. (CC128)

items.name: Land Grab / Land Claim Selection Event
items.desc: Land claim system going live where players link wallets holding land POAs to their account, favorite properties via website tool, then place claims once the event goes live; selection runs by rarity (mythic first) with random selection among ties, moving through smalls to copious plots over roughly 1-2 weeks. Mentioned delivery timing: within 30 days. (CC133)

items.name: Land Grab FAQ Document
items.desc: A document answering community/guild questions about the land grab (already 50% complete) is being prepared for release, to be published around Friday with branding. Mentioned delivery timing: around Friday. (CC133)

items.name: Grid system for zone planning
items.desc: A proprietary grid tool (e.g. region B52) lets teams assign and coordinate art/graphics work per zone, improving efficiency for planning, solidifying, and testing each new zone. (CC38)

items.name: Custom cloud system & sky view
items.desc: A custom, programmatically-moving cloud system has been built giving a panoramic 500km in-game view over Earth from Calido Valley, tied into upcoming lore. (CC51)

items.name: Map Creator Algorithm
items.desc: A map creator algorithm has been developed to randomly generate maps and levels for the mobile game, creating efficiencies and fun level-building methods. (CC33)

items.name: Boats / canoes / kayaks
items.desc: water vehicles for crossing rivers, lakes, and coastal areas (CC1)

items.name: Water system
items.desc: currently players can walk on water (explained in-lore as being frozen by a Quantum Storm). Full water interaction is not yet active (CC1)

items.name: Surface swimming
items.desc: first phase of water interaction; players will be able to swim on top of water. Confirmed as coming before diving (CC1)

items.name: Underwater diving
items.desc: longer-term addition after surface swimming is live; needs a gameplay loop to justify it (e.g. underwater treasure, loot, or creatures). Oxygen/drowning mechanics already prototyped (CC1)

items.name: Water creatures
items.desc: hinted at lurking in bodies of water; adds danger and reason to be cautious when swimming in deep or remote areas (CC1)

items.name: Drowning / health system tie-in
items.desc: oxygen deprivation and drowning confirmed as part of the character health/needs system (CC1)

items.name: World Travel System (Cloud Gate / Sector Travel Ships)
items.desc: large public transport ships used to travel from the home bubble to theme zones without load screens; NPC-piloted; described as limo-style in appearance with a fully built-out interior; can hold approximately 100 players though likely won't carry that many in practice; cloud gates confirmed as the launchers that send players into different areas; highways (shown as green lines on the world map) connect all areas of the world (CC1, CC6, CC8, CC12, CC32, CC50, CC 54)

items.name: Dome entry / docking sequence
items.desc: detailed sequence for entering a dome: fly in, dock/park your vehicle, then walk through a themed lobby into the dome interior; vehicle access gated by the player account syncing with your POA wallet, confirming which vehicles you're permitted to fly (CC54)

items.name: Calido Valley / Calido Resort
items.desc: the central racing and sector hub area; 8km x 8km dedicated zone; the main entry point for new players (CC1)

items.name: Mounts
items.desc: rideable creatures or vehicles with inventory storage capacity; development moved to early next year; quadruped animation significantly more complex than bipeds, requiring unique animation sets per species; still confirmed on roadmap as of CC31 but delayed (CC1, CC17, CC31) (CC31)

items.name: Railway system
items.desc: in-world train network used to transport resources (e.g. corn/biofuel) between zones; featured in the Wild West zone lore and mobile game narrative; trains can be raided as part of gameplay events (CC2)

items.name: World Travel System
items.desc: Public transport pads, cloud gates, and central hubs link sector clusters across Calido and Solace, with vehicles stored in central hangars to skip loading screens. Built as required land-rush infrastructure (Calido → Hub → Solace walkways), then demoed as a multi-stage flow (Calido → cloud gate → sector hub → monorail choice of Solace 1/2/3 → free-roam), targeted for Rare Evo (Aug 15-17, 2024). Shipped as a working Solace 1/2/3--Calido travel loop, later upgraded to support player-owned POA vehicles (including the Juggernaut) for dome-to-dome travel and cross-region goods hauling (Calido → Solace → Esperanza), targeted for summer, with full POA-vehicle flight support following in a near-term build. (CC75, CC79, CC82, CC85, CC94, CC99, CC111, CC115, CC148)

items.name: Public Travel System
items.desc: Large NPC-piloted public transport ships (limo-style interior, ~100-player capacity) move players from the home bubble to theme zones with no load screens, launched via cloud gates and connected by highways (green lines) across the world map. Later extended so players can fly bubble jets/haulers directly between hangars (Calido → Solace → Esperanza) to trade goods across regions, targeted for summer. Mentioned delivery timing: Summer. (CC1, CC6, CC8, CC12, CC32, CC50, CC54, CC148, CC152)

items.name: Flexible Solace Start Locations
items.desc: Confirmed today that a future update will let players choose to start directly in Solace 1, 2, or 3 instead of being forced through the buggy Calido-to-Solace travel route. (CC101)

items.name: Alternate Start Points & Faster POA Travel
items.desc: Future plans confirmed to let players start directly in their own land plot or sector apartment, and to travel via owned POA vehicles faster than public transport, alongside speeding up general public transport. (CC101)

items.name: Jetpacks
items.desc: Zero-G manufacturer's jetpacks, planned in multiple models (e.g. JP 1100) with varying fuel/speed/storage traits, built to let players travel/explore faster and escape danger, releasing with the upcoming sale (CC103). Once live, they let players explore Solace more efficiently (tested around Calido, usable in Rumble Ball) and were used in a community play test flying between checkpoints, including a community-found "bouncing" technique to extend distance. Launch drastically improved Solace/Calido exploration with a bird's-eye view, making large-open-world traversal far easier; holo caches continue to evolve alongside them. Flight was confirmed working in an internal build (Scruffy testing it, including a fall-damage death from flying too high). (CC103, CC107, CC111, CC115, CC142)

items.name: Cargo Terminal / Inventory Transfer System
items.desc: A new cargo terminal system is being built to let players transfer resources from vehicles (e.g., Bubble Jet) to surface stations and land plots, with an in-game currency fee, cheaper for POA owners; inventory system upgrade currently in progress. (CC103)

items.name: Nexus Arrow / Dome Docking System
items.desc: players park or summon their ship/vehicle via Nexus terminals, with each dome/megadome getting separate docking bays for public transport, private vehicles, and larger ships; the flow (park vehicle → travel through lobby → onward into the zone) was first built for the Bubble Jet, designed to replicate across future zones (Esperanza, etc.) with adjusted branding, then staged into a full flight rollout --- showing off ships, flying within Calido airspace, then cloudgate teleport to Solace --- tested with community feedback along the way. (CC1, CC36, CC39, CC107, CC121)

items.name: Aero Trails
items.desc: New traversal/racing trail system with 25 loops built around Calido City requiring boost management and route-finding; showcased live in a competitive race segment and included in the upcoming build. Mentioned delivery timing: This week or pushed to Jan 3rd. (CC115)

items.name: Water Traversal Mechanics
items.desc: Team confirmed swimming, diving underwater, and boats/canoes (previously shown) are in development for crossing water bodies, alongside jetpack crossing already possible. (CC118)

items.name: Calido International Airport
items.desc: Tobias showed the Calido International Airport with large hangar-scale interiors, landing pads for vehicles from bubble jets to Atmos ships, and underground vehicle storage; performance was improved via mesh/batch instancing to reduce draw calls. (CC121)

items.name: Quantum Gate Effects
items.desc: Environment artist Toby mentioned currently helping produce visual effects such as the Quantum Gate as part of ongoing environment art work alongside Solace. (CC93)

items.name: Bubble Jet / Public Transport Travel
items.desc: Confirmed that players without a bubble jet or javelin will need to use public transport, which will be shown in the upcoming land sale video demonstrating in-game travel between zones. (CC5)

items.name: Hoverboard travel item
items.desc: A new leaked image reveals a hoverboard (with matching boots) intended to increase player travel speed, powered by a replaceable nuclear-type core, tied into the game's lore. (CC31)

items.name: Core Mining Loop Design
items.desc: mining levels built internally with public release pending; multiple mining spots across all Solaces and Esperanza; danger increasing the deeper you go with rarer ores/veins at depth; different minerals varying by zone; designed to be engaging rather than a grind. (CC1, CC49)

items.name: Ore Processing & Smelting
items.desc: ore processors outside each mine let players smelt gathered ore into raw ore, then craft it into ingots at a crafting bench; refined further via a flume/Pay Dirt 'double lottery' sifting system; mining processor stations placed near mine entrances. (CC1, CC65, CC126)

items.name: Lumber & Logging Areas
items.desc: dedicated (not free-for-all) tree-chopping zones for environmental reasons, later expanded into more complex gathering mechanics with extra animations, hit points, and processing steps. (CC1, CC48, CC140)

items.name: Rare Minerals
items.desc: minerals like Quanite and Genium exist across rarity tiers up to Mythic, varying by zone. (CC65)

items.name: Mine Shaft Concept Reveal
items.desc: leaked concept art of a mine shaft area with rock structures, pickaxes, gold veins, and mining NPCs Ace, Maria, and Leo. (CC62)

items.name: Mining Rollout Status Updates
items.desc: a recurring string of 'will it make the next build' status checks, plus special hands-on access offered at the POA LV conference. (CC63, CC66, CC67, CC85, CC107, CC133, CC157)

items.name: First Playable Mining Level (Calido Valley)
items.desc: built in about three weeks: open field into a mine shaft, cave systems with multiple veins, five ore types, pickaxe/shovel animations, immersive audio; shown live at Rare Evo in 4K; the same functionality adapted for use across Solace. (CC64)

items.name: Public Testing & Early Expansion
items.desc: released for community testing with headlamps, pickaxes, ore spotting, and rockfalls at deeper levels; holo-caching planned alongside a ~5x area expansion; moved from North Point Hills into Solace 2 for continued testing; North Point Hills demo fully folded into Solace with mining kits (artwork/POAs) in production. (CC68, CC69, CC70, CC75)

items.name: Mining Supply Shop (Jackpot)
items.desc: a dedicated store shown in Cleo Pavilion for buying mining-related assets. (CC74)

items.name: Mining in Solace
items.desc: Commitment & Specific Locations --- confirmed for Solace 2 or 3, promised by Season X/end of year; a specific mine entrance found at Rocky Rapids on Solace One, confirmed to open in Q4. (CC83, CC102, CC103)

items.name: Mines Built Into Solace, Build by Build
items.desc: mines progressively added as explorable areas ahead of full gameplay: confirmed for an upcoming Solace One build; redesigned as a true cave/danger/depth-based-rarity experience requiring mining outfits; unique layouts for Solace 1/2/3 with crouch tunnels, jetpack tweaks, and rock collapses; general updates tested alongside other systems; early exploration-only mines shipped without the full loop; detailed environments with solar-powered processors and hidden 'Farmer Joe' easter eggs across three mines. (CC112, CC124, CC125, CC126, CC127, CC128, CC130, CC132, CC134)

items.name: Meteor Crash Zones
items.desc: a separate resource mechanic where meteor crash sites provide mineral/substance resources. (CC140)

items.name: Ore Gathering & Smelting Quest
items.desc: a dedicated quest line where players mine, smelt, and craft ingots, requiring perk points earned from leveling. (CC151)

items.name: Mining & Logging Resource Gathering (Crafting Tie-In)
items.desc: mining and logging folded into the broader crafting-economy release as the basic resource-gathering loop. (CC153)

items.name: Core Concept & Planning
items.desc: one of the team's most personally anticipated features, confirmed for the Solace MVP; controller mechanics and gameplay planned down to specific inputs, with a long planning document and Unreal blueprints for fish behavior already built; will start simple and grow across seasons, designed to be fun rather than a grind; multiple spots across zones/bodies of water with different fish types, some canoe/kayak-only; a future competitive 'Fishing League' leaderboard referenced. (CC1, CC45, CC49, CC90)

items.name: Development Classification
items.desc: developed in parallel with mining as a resource-flow mini-game, one of the gathering-type loops alongside mining and tree chopping. (CC62, CC65)

items.name: Fish Model & Assets
items.desc: a fully animated fish model (brown trout) completed as proof of concept, shown by David in Discord. (CC63, CC64, CC74)

items.name: Zone Rollout & Performance Scope
items.desc: zone-specific fish planned for Solace, Esperanza, and Fortune before broader content is added; currently limited to marked fishing-icon locations for performance reasons, with a goal to eventually allow fishing in all waters as performance improves. (CC63, CC64, CC75, CC98, CC134)

items.name: Water Tech Integration & Scale
items.desc: tied to the game's water tech, with shore-based and boat-based variations planned, aiming for more fishable square footage than any other fishing game. (CC94)

items.name: Fish Population Simulation
items.desc: the game already simulates three million fish, though not yet catchable by players. (CC146)

items.name: Sight-Fishing / Clear Water Tech
items.desc: new clear-water rendering tech enables testing sight-fishing with visible fish in newly rendered clear water areas. (CC53)

items.name: Core Farming Loop & Food Chain Vision
items.desc: sowing, watering, growing, and harvesting on owned land plots, feeding into cooking and resource systems; over 100 crop types planned with detailed food-chain modelling (raw crops → sandwiches → Michelin-star meals/restaurants); MVP likely starting simple (e.g. corn); soil/fertiliser systems planned. (CC1, CC22, CC46)

items.name: Corn / Biofuel Economy Loop
items.desc: corn grown on player farms produces biofuel powering vehicles like the Bubble Jet and Sprinter, transported via the railway system; a key resource in early Wild West zone lore. (CC2, CC22)

items.name: Farming System Build Status
items.desc: planned for a build after the upcoming one, building on the gathering/inventory/crafting systems, with work starting next year; a working internal loop (plant/grow/nurture/water/harvest) already exists but still needs data-saving integration before it can ship. (CC63, CC64, CC107, CC140, CC157)

items.name: Gathering Prototype
items.desc: an internal multiplayer prototype demonstrated harvesting bushes and storing them in the inventory system. (CC65)

items.name: Berries/Health Prototype
items.desc: an early prototype let players eat berries, with wrong berries causing health loss. (CC74)

items.name: Land Plot Growing & Public Farming Areas
items.desc: players grow crafting ingredients/resources on their own land plots as part of the resource-gathering loop; farming (sowing/watering/growing) will be tied to owned or rented land with in-game-currency costs, while cooking and crafting happen in public town areas. (CC72, CC112)

items.name: Core Crafting System Overview
items.desc: players combine gathered resources into items across an advanced technology-tier tree, either gathered naturally, grown on land plots, or bought from other players; covers craftable backpacks and jetpacks (via grinding, not pay-to-win), building-kit and apartment/land furnishing recipes, a cooking system using farmed/harvested ingredients, and general building-kit construction on player land. (CC1, CC22, CC72, CC106)

items.name: Supply Chain Modelling (Analysts)
items.desc: a team of analysts mapping detailed supply chains for hundreds of in-game items (raw materials through processing to finished products), using bread as a worked example (wheat → flour → bakery → bread); roughly 6 months in as of the initial report with 6-12 months remaining, simplified for gameplay while retaining educational depth; a junior analyst was hired to assist. (CC22, CC23)

items.name: Perk System
items.desc: players earn 1 perk point per season level-up, unlocking crafting abilities (e.g. required to craft ingots), with more perk types planned. (CC1)

items.name: Skill Trees
items.desc: a traditional RPG skill tree system was scrapped in favor of interaction-based 'metaverse mechanics,' where gathering/crafting actions use realistic timed motions (e.g. a timed swing at peak intensity to chop a tree) rather than menu-driven skill points. (CC4, CC48)

items.name: Inventory System
items.desc: an inventory system in development, tying into character stats and skill mechanics. (CC74)

items.name: Crafting System Rollout Status Updates
items.desc: a recurring string of build-status updates on the core crafting system: interface built but held back pending a database/inventory rework; a detailed crafting-and-economics system with an estimated ~4-month build starting soon; work resuming after the Solace world-travel release; station updates tested in-build; conversion from single-player to multiplayer; and a first working iteration linking crafting to mining, questing, and combat. (CC75, CC85, CC99, CC124, CC127, CC128, CC130, CC131, CC132, CC133, CC136, CC137, CC140, CC145, CC146)

items.name: In-Apartment Crafting
items.desc: players can craft (e.g. woodworking at a carpenter's table) inside their personal apartment within the Sector Resort system. (CC82)

items.name: Crafting Progression & Tiered Benches
items.desc: tiered crafting benches (tier 1 fits in an apartment, tier 2 is larger with multiple benches) with specialization leveling (~15 routes) unlocking bigger benches, blueprints, reduced failure rates, and eventually automated factories; reduced-tier access available to free-to-play players via town centers. (CC84, CC125)

items.name: Crafting Buildings (Town Structures)
items.desc: dedicated crafting buildings (stonemason, blacksmith, carpenter, artisan, textiles, chef, farming/agriculture/botany), two per town, with future builds adding science buildings (electronics, biology, chemistry, physics). (CC119)

items.name: Weapon Attachment System
items.desc: players can craft, buy, or trade non-POA weapon attachments (magazines, barrels, scopes, suppressors) that visually and functionally upgrade a base POA weapon while keeping its color scheme. (CC123)

items.name: Gathering Mechanics (Tree Chopping, Logging & Tools)
items.desc: a raw-material processing pipeline (trees → lumber, corn → food/biofuel) feeding building and vehicle systems, including a dedicated logging area where players chop regrowing trees and feed logs through a machine into lumber planks; tools like axes require parts gathered from different zones; a custom chaos-physics tree-chopping mechanic (beyond Unreal's built-in physics) adds realistic breakage based on hit strength/angle and a falling-tree risk, with power-bar mechanics planned to scale to mining and fishing too. (CC3, CC4, CC48, CC100, CC102)

items.name: Secret Recipe Fix / Hotfix
items.desc: a missing secret-recipe ingredient (a misplaced/oversized bush prop) was fixed and made findable; questing launched with 3 recipes including this one. (CC148)

items.name: Recipe Count Growth
items.desc: crafting recipes grew from an initial 3 to 374 (multi-tier system combining raw materials into intermediate items), then past 400 --- including a town-foundation quest to smelt ore into ingots --- across 12 active benches at tiers 1-3 of 5 planned, ultimately reaching about 429 combinations. (CC148, CC150, CC151, CC152, CC153, CC155, CC156)

items.name: Quest Terminals (Civic Works)
items.desc: orange terminal buildings placed in every town across all Solaces and Kid Toledo City (3 in KTC, 1 in the pavilion, 1 per Solace town), triggering quests based on season level or prior quest completion. (CC1, CC151)

items.name: Relic Quest
items.desc: a large cross-Solace find-and-seek quest tied to shipwreck/crash-site lore: ships crash-landed scattering cargo, and players locate ~30-40 relics (mythic/legendary/rare/uncommon items like a Fabergé egg, samurai sword, or Polaroid camera) and sell them to an antique shop on the global map; originally tied to a collab that was delayed. In-game items only, not POAs. (CC1, CC150, CC154)

items.name: Core Quest & Tasking Architecture
items.desc: a compass-driven tasking system (similar to Skyrim/New World) guides players to objectives, with main/side quests on the compass display, XP/season-level rewards, quest triggers based on prior quests/level/inventory, cross-level quests (e.g. gather in Solace, craft in Toledo, sell in the city), daily/repeatable tasks (mine, chop, fish, race), and an optional (not forced) quest system alongside free-roam exploration; the compass itself carries over from earlier build testing into Solace for quests and district navigation. (CC1, CC12, CC61, CC72)

items.name: Town/Settlement Crafting Quest Loop
items.desc: a guided quest teaching the crafting system through an ore-gathering → smelting → ingot-crafting loop, expanded into a fuller three-part grinding chain per town (gather raw ingredients, craft intermediate goods, craft final items to sell), estimated 15-20 hours of gameplay with plans for 3-5 towns. (CC1, CC150)

items.name: Partner Quests
items.desc: future collaborative quests with Cardano projects (World Mobile, Hosky, etc.) and other communities (Base, etc.), with a dashboard tracking completions and enabling partner airdrops; on hold until the market is more active. (CC1)

items.name: Player-Created Delivery Quests
items.desc: a planned system letting players create their own delivery/fetch quests for other players (e.g. deliver an item to an apartment door or land plot) in exchange for in-game rewards; described as 'definitely coming.' (CC1, CC152)

items.name: Progression, XP & Skill Tree Backend
items.desc: a flexible backend for achievements, progression, and skill trees (six months in development) letting devs create roles/recipes/staged tasks in real time, with ~12 starting skills unlocking new tasks based on player actions; XP, perk points, and skill trees are already built into the game but not yet turned on or fully integrated. (CC80, CC147)

items.name: Rich Quests & AI-Driven Dialogue
items.desc: plans to heavily invest in rich, multi-stage quests involving AI NPCs, lore progression, and dozens of quests over the year, alongside basic gather-type quests; the team was researching quest/dialogue systems with plans to use AI for dialogue generation and, eventually, fully real-time AI-driven quest conversations. (CC116, CC117)

items.name: Onboarding Quest System
items.desc: an hour-long guided intro quest with an NPC guide, starting gear, cinematic 'beats' and AAA-style cutscenes, with a skip option, rolling out partially then fully by the rift/alpha release; shipped as a first version teaching clothes/credits/ACMs/the journey store via quest terminals with 6-8 find/collect quests (~4-6 hours) in Kid Toledo/Pavilion, using in-engine cutscene-style level sequences that retain player control; expanded into a scalable system with full cinematics teaching controls, credit chips, the need system and medical system, plus a demo-apartment security-droid challenge for added stealth difficulty; a second onboarding pass followed. (CC144, CC145, CC146, CC147, CC150)

items.name: Quest Audio Hotfix
items.desc: fixed a bug where quest sound triggers were audible to everyone on the map instead of just the player. (CC148)

items.name: Quest System Rework (Discoverable Quests)
items.desc: experimenting with breaking linear quests into more discoverable, interconnected ones, tested internally; uncertain timing due to additional audio/content rework needed. (CC149)

items.name: Quest Chains & Profile Customization Rewards
items.desc: completing staged quest chains (e.g. 10 trails to become a 'rookie') unlocks profile customization rewards like icons, banners, and titles; currently in planning. (CC149)

items.name: New Player Tour Quest System
items.desc: a quest system guiding new players around the game world, reducing the need for manual community tours. (CC153)

items.name: Civic Works Quest Count Growth
items.desc: the questing system expanded from onboarding cinematics to 97 total quests (~80 non-onboarding), chained together at varying difficulty tied to progression and IGC rewards, then grew further with 34 more quests added, bringing the total to about 133. (CC155, CC156)

items.name: Cargo Hauling (Holage) Missions
items.desc: career-based hauling quests starting at the voyage terminal in Kid Toledo Valley, expanding cross-world to Solace and hubs as players level up their hauling skill. (CC155)

items.name: Rift Mechanics
items.desc: Core System --- rifts open across the world (treated like weather-alert world events), spawning creatures that must be fought off and shut down using Anchor Stones and Time Stones, with a final 'heart of the rift' loot box on closing; creatures escalate in difficulty the longer a rift is left unchecked; rewards (IGC/XP/Infinity) are distributed based on each player's contribution to prevent late 'kill stealing.' (CC1, CC123, CC138, CC148, CC157)

items.name: Rift Enemies & Creatures
items.desc: the enemy roster: Quantum Monsters generally, light/medium/heavy armored Terra Drone variants, a Heavy Enforcer (part robot/organic), a small poison-needle 'Mer/Jab' variant, light/medium/heavy mechs, and a giant elephant-like 'Dread Frame' boss appearing at the end of battles. (CC1, CC125, CC137, CC142, CC145, CC146, CC147, CC148)

items.name: Rift Development & Release Timeline
items.desc: a recurring string of status updates on when rifts and full rift combat will ship, generally tracking toward 'this year' and the alpha/rift release window, developed in parallel with other combat and world systems throughout. (CC109, CC128, CC131, CC132, CC133, CC140, CC142, CC145, CC148, CC150, CC153)

items.name: Weapons Technology & Systems
items.desc: multiple damage types (ballistic, pulse/energy, charge/reactor, beam, and Quantum weapons specifically effective against Quantum Monsters), a dynamic performance metric (DIPS R30) replacing simple DPS, primary/secondary weapon slots with quick-swap, and a planned weapon wear/maintenance system as a later 'cherry on top' feature. (CC1, CC17, CC121, CC124)

items.name: Named Weapons & POA Sales
items.desc: the weapon-drop line: the Mythic Double Dragon laser pistol (and matching turret) as the first reveal, followed by a phased ballistic/pulse sale across manufacturer brands (Bourne & Lee, Cumaru Defense, Rando's Metal Works, Asuna Arms, Superverse, Frontier Arms), the Meat Grinder shotgun, Kamaru Defense Outlaw, SK47, an Old World Provisions shotgun, and the Caesar 556 assault rifle. (CC14, CC17, CC119, CC122, CC123, CC145, CC146, CC147, CC153)

items.name: Weapon Audio & Cinematics
items.desc: high-quality weapon-reveal cinematics paired with real recorded firearm audio (shots, shell drops from actual guns) rather than stock sound effects. (CC122, CC123)

items.name: Combat Mechanics
items.desc: Core --- flying-while-shooting with jetpacks, early staging builds with no damage yet, motion-matching integrated with the Avatar 3.0 skeleton, armor/backpack loadouts and gear-weight affecting movement speed, ragdoll physics on death, inventory-risk/loot-penalty on death (especially near rifts), and a basic-needs/health system tracking fall and combat damage --- building up into a working, QA-tested multiplayer combat system. (CC1, CC118, CC121, CC123, CC124, CC126, CC127, CC128, CC129, CC130, CC131, CC132, CC139, CC140, CC141, CC147)

items.name: Multiplayer Combat QA
items.desc: the replicated multiplayer combat system moved through active bug-fixing (e.g. gun-fire sync issues) toward a stable build. (CC125)

items.name: Shooting Ranges & Combat Practice
items.desc: Terror Tunnels and shooting ranges built across multiple Solaces, expanded with a gun store/shop and moving-target practice areas that gather server-side hit feedback ahead of full rift release. (CC1, CC118, CC119, CC120, CC123, CC124, CC132)

items.name: Ammo Stations & Weapon Shops
items.desc: map-marked shops and stations where players can buy ammo and load up weapons. (CC132)

items.name: PvP Modes & Arenas
items.desc: the PvP mode roster, released and iterated across multiple builds: an early general PvP plan, a maintenance-tunnel arena, Capture the Flag, Team Death Match, Hot Zone (v2, red vs blue platform-claiming), Quantum Rush, Three Bridges, and Last Team Standing, with a third mode in testing. (CC1, CC51, CC144, CC149, CC150, CC151, CC153, CC154, CC155, CC156, CC157)

items.name: Safe Zones & Bounty System
items.desc: towns generate a protective 'influence sphere,' with a bounty system triggered by killing players in safe zones --- flagged players can be hunted by other players or security bots/drones without consequence. (CC119, CC150, CC153, CC155)

items.name: Prison System
items.desc: a mechanic for players who commit crimes (killing outside safe zones), including fines/restitution and eventual transport to prison with tasks required to get out; tied to the rift release. (CC145, CC155)

items.name: Cornucopias Labs (PvP Testing Facility)
items.desc: a facility in Calido Valley Resort for testing various systems, potentially including PvP. (CC75)

items.name: Custom Dome PVP Demo
items.desc: a live gameplay demo of a PvP shooter mode inside a Custom Dome bunker map with turret drones and red-vs-blue team combat. (CC21)

items.name: PvP/PvE Battle Functionality (Pets)
items.desc: battling functionality in active development in response to community interest in pet battles. (CC51)

items.name: GTI, Javelin & Sprinter (Original Lineup)
items.desc: the GTI and Javelin/Sprinter were among the first racing POA mints; the Javelin racing game itself was ported from UE4 to UE5 (a full world-partitioning rebuild plus a new wheel physics system and multiplayer added, confirmed complete). The GTI Javelin sale suffered severe minting technical issues, so the team gave away all Javelins free to everyone in the queue --- a giveaway valued at over $1M. The Sprinter/Javelin sale itself completed as part of Q1 2022 roadmap milestones, and the Javelin later shipped as a complete, viewable-in-showroom legendary A-class vehicle positioned as the Bonanza's rival. (CC1, CC3, CC23, CC25, CC29, CC58)

items.name: F9R / Valkyrie F9R (S-Class)
items.desc: an S-Class racer with blazing speed comparable to the Jester; revealed on display in Cleo Pavilion, added to the racing menu with a limited player demo drive (Feb 2nd), tested by many players, then given its first POA sale --- first on Ethereum, later its first sale on the Base chain. (CC1, CC74, CC77, CC78, CC87, CC103)

items.name: Bubble Jet S-Class
items.desc: a separate S-Class vehicle POA, distinct from the OG custom Bubble Jet, sold in the store sale. (CC1, CC103)

items.name: T3 Valley Raceworks
items.desc: a Formula One-style vintage racer, very fast but single-occupancy with no cargo space, already minted and in players' wallets; later redesigned 20-30% larger with an F-14/stealth-bomber-inspired look and unique rarity-based interior trims, race-ready for its sale; balancing tweaks made against T1A and other vehicles. (CC29, CC58, CC71)

items.name: The Jester (X-Class)
items.desc: the highest-tier vehicle class, never sold, only earnable through gameplay progression and tournament success; described as very fast and powerful. (CC1, CC103)

items.name: New X-Class Racer
items.desc: a separate, purchasable X-Class racer (same class as the Jester), extremely fast and difficult to fly, released in the Christmas sale. (CC146)

items.name: Astro / Core Dynamics 4
items.desc: a B-class sporty courier-type vehicle with large cargo capacity, introduced into the C-class lineup alongside the Bubblejet Sprinter and T1, also used for zone-to-zone travel. (CC57, CC58, CC98)

items.name: Bonanza
items.desc: vehicle artwork revealed for the Bubblejet-manufactured Bonanza, planned for sale shortly after the racing game's launch with accompanying lore; ongoing production confirmed alongside other vehicle types. (CC49, CC68)

items.name: Super Phantom & Sunset Speeder
items.desc: two new racers added in the Quantum Autumn build: the Bubble Jet Super Phantom (S-Class, positioned to compete with the F9R, released for sale via ADA/USDC with 1,500 units) and the Rando's Metalworks Sunset Speeder (A-Class surface-faction racer), later resurfacing for marketplace resale. (CC106, CC109, CC110, CC114)

items.name: Juggernaut (Cargo Ship)
items.desc: a large 82m cargo-class POA with 16 cargo modules across five rarities; slipped past the December build pending model completion and the World Travel System vehicle upgrade, then sold in a limited five-rarity sale across Cardano and Base ($350, 760 total supply, whitelist tier for top corn-point holders), with the finished asset still being built out for delivery in upcoming builds. (CC111, CC112, CC113)

items.name: Atlas (Large Ship POA)
items.desc: the first large-ship POA sale; in-game utility for holders still pending, remains purchasable on Base though not currently listed. (CC115)

items.name: Shinobi X
items.desc: a new racer added to a seasonal sale and the next build, confirmed fun to drive and faster than previous vehicles once live. (CC146, CC147)

items.name: New Cargo Vehicle (Christmas Sale)
items.desc: a limited-quantity cargo vehicle about half the size of the Juggernaut. (CC146)

items.name: T1 (Free Racing Vehicle)
items.desc: a free, track-provided C-class vehicle (plus a beefed-up A-class version) used only for racing at Calido Valley, not ownable/flyable elsewhere; tested against the F9R on new tracks. (CC1, CC58, CC104)

items.name: OG Custom Sprinter
items.desc: a limited-quantity aftermarket-customized Sprinter with its own sound system and branding. (CC58)

items.name: Free Flying Vehicle (No-POA Racer)
items.desc: a free, less-polished/slower vehicle any player can race without owning an POA. (CC36)

items.name: OG Bubblejet POA
items.desc: the very first POA mint for Cornucopias, later expanded from 9,000 to 12,400 supply to spread ownership while preserving rarity tiers. (CC1)

items.name: Vehicle Systems & Mechanics
items.desc: the shared mechanical layer: a weight system (backpack/armor loadouts affecting speed), a class system (A/B/C, tested via real-world-style speed/acceleration/braking/handling), collision physics, damage/repair/fuel systems (fuel earned via staking/farming/IGC), a medical-center respawn system on destruction, vehicle wraps and wear-and-tear, garage upgrades, 3D viewing/customization, light kits, explosion-physics testing, cargo/inventory capacity (standard cargo-unit measurement), per-vehicle dashboards/gauges, an add-on tech system for flying vehicles, and a Bubblehead-POA display holder accessory. (CC1, CC12, CC25, CC29, CC33, CC37, CC41, CC42, CC43, CC45, CC46, CC55, CC57, CC58)

items.name: Jetpacks
items.desc: Zero-G's hoverboards (their original pre-jetpack product) evolved into multiple jetpack types (Zero-G Stratos, Solace Explorer, Rando's Junker Jet) with distinct speed/fuel/storage stats and a Quantum Compression fuel mechanic, craftable through grinding. Jetpacks moved from 'nearly ready, pending animations' (cutting Solace/Cedo travel time from ~45 minutes to ~5) to a released traversal system, followed by mine-specific animations, new GTI animations, a lag-fix, and new purchasable IGC jetpack types (Core Dynamics Glide Sport, Alien X) plus a single-thruster Thrust Commander jetpack. (CC1, CC31, CC106, CC109, CC110, CC126, CC132, CC137, CC139, CC146, CC153)

items.name: Cargo/Hauling Vehicles & Mounts
items.desc: a cargo-transport layer built on the same high-speed multiplayer networking as racing, including a built-out cargo hauler area/vehicles ('orcas'), zone-to-zone travel POA vehicles (Javelin, Bubble Jet, Banza, Astro 4), public vehicle landing bays, the Bubble Jet Strat Lifter Hauler, H2 Load Runner mount, and Cloud Barge cargo vehicle from Randos for bulk hub-city trade, plus a new cargo pack accessory. (CC65, CC66, CC68, CC98, CC127, CC145, CC146, CC153)

items.name: Additional Vehicle Content
items.desc: a bubble jet showroom displaying multiple rarity tiers with functioning security/tractor-beam vehicles active in the world; the Valley Race Works manufacturer building (branded Copi Cafe vehicle plus free 1989-model cars for players without their own vehicle); a player-controllable exploration companion/vehicle in development; and new utility drones (recon, TV/spectator, racing modes) with a backpack-deploy mechanic. Also includes a GTI manufacturer vehicle showroom (containing an X-Wing/Batmobile-style concept vehicle) shown during a community visit, at the time closed off to the public. (CC51, CC52, CC60, CC156, CC157)

items.name: Holo/Hollow Caches
items.desc: a hide-and-seek hologram-cache collectible system (~100 caches, common to Mythic rarity) originally used to gamify testing engagement in Calido/Cedo Resort; expanded with puzzles (find-and-seek, escape rooms, jump/parkour), new Mythic hoard caches, and periodic full revamps/refreshes of cache count and locations. Built out into a full game loop with leaderboards and moved from exploitable local saves to server-side saving. (CC1, CC61, CC62, CC63, CC67, CC80, CC81, CC87, CC89, CC111, CC128, CC132)

items.name: Rumble Ball
items.desc: a physics-based, portable soccer-style mini-game with no formal rules, first revealed and played live; added as a recurring venue across the world. Iterated repeatedly: bouncier ball, size/multiball changes, dribbling/shooting/passing/lobbing mechanics, a 100+ line announcer, knockback physics from community feedback, and passing added via community-driven updates. (CC1, CC74, CC78, CC80, CC128, CC130, CC132, CC154, CC156, CC157)

items.name: Aero Trails
items.desc: a jetpack-based timed ring-course game loop in a brutalist city area of Calido Valley; expanded with new courses across Solace 1/2/3 and Calido (each course distinct, with leaderboards), plus an easier onboarding starter course in the Pavilion/Esperanza area. (CC1, CC114, CC130, CC132, CC149)

items.name: Hot Zones
items.desc: a red-vs-blue platform/zone-capturing PvP mode with jetpacks and guns; reworked into 'Hot Zone Speedrunner' (capture-the-flag style team racing) and a fully revamped version enabling jetpacks/guns for zone-claiming. (CC1, CC139, CC149, CC150, CC153)

items.name: Shooting Alley/Gallery
items.desc: a timed shooting mini-game in weapon-shop basements on the global map with easy/hard/impossible difficulty gated by season level, later enhanced with moving human/bullseye targets, opening windows, a quest giver, and overhead targets tied to community feedback. (CC1, CC150, CC151, CC153, CC157)

items.name: Delivery Quest ('Crazy Taxi')
items.desc: a DoorDash-style timed delivery quest starting at Burger Barn, picking up and dropping off orders across multiple in-world fast-food shops (Burrito Boss, etc.) against the clock; iterated with a drop-off puzzle/code element, follow-marker camera improvements, and difficulty tuning on the related drone-delivery puzzle. (CC1, CC151, CC152, CC153, CC154, CC155, CC157)

items.name: Inventory System
items.desc: multiple inventory approaches were prototyped (3D mesh-based, jigsaw/space-based, slot-based) before settling on an actively-developed system with persistent server-side data storage, released ahead of dev holidays and core to gathering/questing/item management, with plans for backpack, mount, home storage, and transport integration. (CC65, CC66, CC83, CC115)

items.name: Gathering & Resource Mini-Loops
items.desc: tree chopping, wood chopping, and logging built out as dedicated entrance/onboarding mini-activities and public gathering areas (with respawning trees), developed alongside hunting/gathering and mining for the Solace/Esperanza land experience, plus Cornucopias Labs test builds for wood/rock chopping and fishing, vending-machine and trading interactions, and scavenger-hunt content spread across Solace's large explorable map. (CC39, CC45, CC46, CC49, CC65, CC68, CC85, CC99, CC104, CC116, CC117, CC140, CC157)

items.name: Needs & Survival System
items.desc: a survival mechanic tracking hunger/thirst (requiring drinking/eating or taking damage), stamina/fatigue affected by inventory weight and environment, and a human-body simulation (heart rate, blood, tiredness, energy); includes an eating mechanic, ragdoll-physics death/fall system, medical centers for healing, and a related fall/need system for mine hazards. (CC17, CC65, CC74, CC118, CC126, CC140, CC141, CC142)

items.name: Player Progression & Specialization
items.desc: a progression screen with XP, levels, and perk points feeding long-term specialization/skill trees for professions like fishing, mining, woodworking, and shotguns, alongside broader MMORPG-style character stats. (CC97, CC148)

items.name: Character Movement System
items.desc: a new movement system shipped including auto hero-landings, forward rolls after flying, and parkour spin moves over railings. (CC131, CC132)

items.name: Quality-of-Life Additions
items.desc: small additions like a player-toggleable light for dark areas, hidden (not-yet-active) logging/mining areas placed in-world for future content, and a confirmed exploration backpack item to help players explore. (CC100, CC102)

items.name: Alpha Milestone & Primary Game Loop
items.desc: reaching Alpha status by year's end, and completing the primary/foundational game loop, were both confirmed as major year-end goals requiring many gameplay systems to be in place first. (CC47, CC116)

items.name: Custom Dome Mini Games
items.desc: future player-created game experiences (racing, PvP, delivery, etc.) in player-owned domes. (CC1)

items.name: Community Jetpack Checkpoint Play Test
items.desc: a community play test with ~25-30 players, flying to designated checkpoints on Solace as a foreshadow/format test for future gameplay, also used for cross-region performance testing. (CC111)

items.name: Leaderboards
items.desc: leaderboards were added into the game this year as part of major releases. (CC115)

items.name: Terror Tunnels
items.desc: Indiana Jones-style obstacle/shooting courses with multiple tunnels and a harder second stage (tight beams, crouching through vents); a possible third stage undecided; remains in-game as a permanent target-practice activity. (CC124)

items.name: Drone Shooting
items.desc: a drone shooting activity accidentally revealed as part of upcoming build content. (CC128)

items.name: Loot System (Hybrid)
items.desc: a hybrid loot system combining individual world loot drops, vending machine purchases, and crafting-based loot. (CC130)

items.name: Prison System
items.desc: players who accrue bounties and are killed are sent to prison, featuring its own mini-game content players may deliberately seek out; artwork in progress, planned for a future build after the apartment release. (CC150, CC153)

items.name: Relics Collection & Antique Shop
items.desc: players collect relics in Solace and sell them at the antique shop. (CC156)

items.name: In-Game Music/Concert Experience
items.desc: a prototype nightclub/stage lets players choose tracks by walking into certain areas, using music from an artist who granted permission for in-game use, shown at Consensus. (CC10)

items.name: GTI Javelin & Bubble Jet POA Scoring Multiplier
items.desc: the mobile Tower Defense game incorporates GTI Javelin and Bubble Jet POAs affecting the player's scoring multiplier. (CC15)

items.name: Character Launchpad Mechanic
items.desc: a launchpad that launches a character's avatar through the air. (CC16)

items.name: Find Farmer Joe / Solace Demo
items.desc: a hide-and-seek mini-game demo shown at cPOAcon with a leaderboard tracking who found Joe first, whose location is randomly assigned each playthrough. (CC28)

items.name: Frisco Arcade Machine
items.desc: a random arcade machine introduced alongside the fur babies reveal. (CC32)

items.name: Wildlife System
items.desc: passive animals (bears, foxes, deer, wolves, mountain lions, coyotes) roaming Solace and Esperanza, with hundreds of creature types planned and thousands roaming per zone, differing by region (whitetail deer/bear/mountain lion for Esperanza; deer/brown bear/coyote/fox for Solace), usable in crafting; includes water creatures hinted for aquatic/coastal zones and early animal capture/harvesting mechanics. Development included statue-style hub models per sector's signature animal, a dedicated creatures artist hire, cows tied to Burger Barn lore, a completed wildlife roster (bear, white-tailed deer, mountain lion, gray wolf, coyote, two fox variants, trout) built with procedural micro-detail materials and efficient poly budgets, and working AI behavior (e.g. a bear showing hunger/interest before chasing deer). (CC1, CC13, CC17, CC20, CC76, CC83, CC85, CC92, CC102, CC106, CC116, CC118, CC119, CC121)

items.name: Rift Creatures
items.desc: the enemy roster spawned from rifts, including Quantum Creatures generally and named designs: the Jab/Injector (a wingless mosquito-like melee enemy), a Humanoid Mech (light/medium/heavy, organic-mechanical, nanite-rigged, with a vulnerable neck/back weak point), the Mer/'Blueberry Butt Spider' (a slow charge-attacker), the Hopper (a tripod sniper-type that flees while shooting), and a giant elephant-like rift boss that appears after waves of other enemies are cleared. (CC1, CC138)

items.name: Additional Named Creatures
items.desc: further specific creature reveals including an early fish model and unspecified larger creatures shown internally, a giant codenamed 'Elephant' creature (~5x the size of the largest character, AT-AT-like presence), and a fox with walk/run/idle locomotion animations (player-controllable during testing), potentially as a companion or hunted creature. (CC76, CC147, CC149, CC150)

items.name: Pets & Mounts
items.desc: confirmed '100% on the roadmap' as a surprise community reveal, with all pet types to be announced/released together rather than staggered; pushed to early the following year due to the animation complexity of multi-legged creatures, with NPC animal/pet work and remaining programmatic AI targeted for 2026. Fur babies (companion creatures) were introduced separately as an early community reveal. (CC3, CC13, CC17, CC31, CC32, CC51, CC146)

items.name: Core Apartment Offering
items.desc: every player gets a free starter apartment (bedroom/kitchen/studio) claimed by browsing available units, upgradeable to larger spaces with IGC/Copi; built on a shared full builder tool (600-1,000+ assets) also used for land building and Custom Domes, supporting up to 50,000 apartments per global hub with persistent cross-region data and a Sector Resort/home-bubble redesign (basement-to-penthouse progression). (CC1, CC6, CC82, CC99, CC124)

items.name: Builder Tool
items.desc: Technical Development --- the actual construction tool: a snapping wall/floor/ceiling/kitchen system that went through multiple full rewrites (reaching version 4+ after earlier plugin approaches failed), migrated from a sub-project into the main build, survived a UE5.5→5.6 engine upgrade, and grew to a ~485-1,000+ piece customization kit (materials, finishes, colors); QA setbacks due to scale/complexity were later resolved. (CC126, CC128, CC131, CC133, CC137, CC140, CC146, CC147, CC150, CC153)

items.name: Backend Performance & Scale
items.desc: repeated architecture overhauls to handle tens of thousands of player-owned spaces: moving from pure cloud calls to local server-side caching, then to near-player loading with claim indicators, ultimately restoring ~120 FPS after early performance issues from loading 100,000+ apartments at once. (CC1, CC148, CC149, CC151, CC154)

items.name: Apartment Tiers & Sizes
items.desc: the tier system revealed in stages: Solace apartment blocks (free 10x10m starter, larger 10x20/20x20 options), a free 'Basic A' 100sqm plot, then a full Basic/Plus/Prime/Elite/Pinnacle ladder doubling in size each tier (Prime at 400sqm/4 stories, Elite at 800sqm/2 floors), with Solace hub supporting ~50,000 apartments (expandable to 100,000) and similar capacity planned elsewhere. (CC126, CC134, CC135, CC136, CC137)

items.name: Sale Events Timeline
items.desc: a recurring string of premium/Strata apartment sale announcements, each timed near the land grab for marketing synergy and repeatedly pushed back as the builder tool matured. (CC130, CC131, CC132, CC133, CC141, CC145)

items.name: Building Kits & Themes
items.desc: decor/theme kits releasing in waves: a Modern/Contemporary base kit and a Mountain Cabin kit (slanted ceilings, log wall covers, harvest decor) shown side by side, premium Cyberpunk and Cabin kits in production, interior showcase videos, and later Summer Art, Club After Hours, Retro Pop, and Neon Vibes kits, with more planned. (CC133, CC135, CC137, CC140, CC143, CC155, CC156)

items.name: Claiming & Furnishing User Flow
items.desc: the actual player experience: a real estate office/showroom terminal for viewing and claiming units, an empty-apartment walkthrough video showing the starting blank slate, a dedicated customization tool for moving walls/furniture/paintings, and in-game testing of the claim-to-furnish flow (building lists, floor navigation via the new pointer system, entering furnish mode). (CC137, CC138, CC142, CC144, CC152)

items.name: Elevators & Storage Infrastructure
items.desc: multiplayer-replicated elevators built into the apartment infrastructure, plus apartment stash storage letting players store inventory items inside their space. (CC149, CC156)

items.name: Launch & Expansion Plans
