items.desc: the system shipped as the centerpiece 'Coming Home 0.4.0' release (May 22nd) with home-building for Solace, followed by hotfixes (duplicating inventory, slow loading); the same builder tech is now confirmed as the stepping-stone being adapted for land-plot building, with Esperanza and Fortune planned to get their own apartment hubs like Solace. (CC155, CC156, CC157)

items.name: Size Reveals (Progressive, 2022)
items.desc: five plot sizes revealed one at a time over several episodes: Small (16m×24m, ~an NBA court), Medium (36m×24m, ~a baseball infield), Large (32m×48m, ~an Olympic pool), Epic (~an American football field), and Copious (64m×96m, ~a Premier League pitch); each available across five rarity tiers (common→mythic), guaranteeing the same plot size regardless of rarity. Plots are hand-placed within zones, not laid out on a uniform grid. Note: sizes were confirmed to have nearly doubled from original plans after the team adopted UE5, while prices stayed the same. (CC5, CC6, CC7, CC8, CC9)

items.name: First Land Sale Event (Copious, 2022)
items.desc: a five-day, role-gated sale (OG members → vehicle POA holders → 30+ day Discord members → public), with Mythic land price cut 30%; completed successfully as 20 total tiered sales, and demoed live to the community and IOHK at the Consensus conference. (CC1, CC2, CC4, CC9, CC10, CC11)

items.name: Property Designations
items.desc: plots can be designated residential, commercial, agricultural (farm), or mixed-use depending on size; ranching/livestock (even on the smallest plot) and running a merchant shop are both confirmed viable uses. (CC3, CC5)

items.name: Inn/Rental & Tenancy System
items.desc: players can build upward and rent rooms to other players (letting renters replenish stats without returning home), or rent out land plots for a season with renewal options set by the landowner; this requires active engagement, not passive income. (CC3, CC42)

items.name: Modular Kit Themes
items.desc: mix-and-match modular kit themes (modern commercial, tropical, EDM, and more) usable together within a single dome, with POA-exclusive decoration meshes tied to specific POAs (e.g. Bubble Jet owners get Bubble Jet meshes), player-importable images, and planned future kits (lighting, zone-themed, racing) sold separately on the marketplace alongside custom dome POA bundles. (CC1, CC20, CC21, CC23, CC25)

items.name: Unified Building System
items.desc: one shared, precise snap-based 'level builder' system powers apartments, land plots, and Custom Domes together; the system extends the apartment builder to open-world land plots (larger prefabs/decor at scale), requiring more performance testing than apartments and following lessons learned from that build. (CC99, CC124, CC126, CC134)

items.name: Terraforming
items.desc: early stages confirmed; players reshape their land plots. (CC1, CC12, CC20)

items.name: Building Tool Early Development
items.desc: an agile-built home construction tool (floors, walls, windows, doors, materials) was demoed at ~25% complete, later rebuilt from a UE4 prototype into UE5 with multi-template support; an alpha release for a small test group was targeted 5-6 months out at the time. (CC6, CC7, CC15)

items.name: Crafting & Industry Buildings
items.desc: named utility buildings players can place on land: Electronics Factory (raw materials → electronics), Blacksmith (metal goods), General Store, Wood Shop (workbench-to-industrial progression), and Sawmill/Ore Processor (outperforming public/free versions); buildings come in multiple upgrade levels, with higher levels needing larger plots. (CC1, CC3, CC6, CC65, CC84, CC102, CC113)

items.name: Blueprint Buy/Sell Economy
items.desc: players design structures in the builder tool, which become purchasable blueprints; buyers gather materials and build them at theme zones themselves --- a core build-to-earn mechanic, with pre-built templates also planned for non-builders. (CC6)

items.name: Personal Bubble Starter State & Hangar
items.desc: every player's personal bubble starts with two trees and a hammock by default; a vehicle hangar area beneath the bubble (park vehicle, access main bubble through it) was demoed internally multiple times before public reveal. Owners of the Jet Chicken collector POA can additionally bring a 3D model into their bubble space. (CC6, CC12, CC19, CC32, CC34, CC35)

items.name: System Design & Access Planning
items.desc: town/district layout finalized (12 towns/sector, ~222 plots/town, hand-placed), plot rarity determined by pick order (not pre-assigned) via an in-game hologram scanner tool, access-permission controls for landowners, and confirmation that both physical in-game exploration and a companion website map would be used together for selection. (CC54, CC62, CC63, CC71, CC72, CC78, CC82, CC83)

items.name: The 2024 Three-Zone Timeline (Solace/Esperanza/Fortuna)
items.desc: As Originally Promised --- the plan laid out mid-2024: Solace land rush targeted Q3, Esperanza (built simultaneously with Solace) also targeted Q3 as a second rush, and Fortuna targeted Q4 --- completing all nine domes' land rushes by end of year. An POA-swap decision (new POA vs. reusing the existing blank land POA) was still pending at this point. (CC85)

items.name: Website & Backend Build-Out
items.desc: a dedicated land grab website (separate from the game client) was built by Michael, pulling all Solace land plots onto the site ahead of the event, alongside a plot reader/coordinate tool, pre-grab terrain fixes (flattening, lighting, points of interest), and a public Land Map Selection Tool for favoriting properties ahead of time. (CC91, CC95, CC97, CC98, CC99, CC101, CC116)

items.name: Claim Algorithm & Rarity System Development
items.desc: the selection algorithm (rarity-weighted, mythic-to-common priority, random tie-breaks, ~75-second cadence over roughly two weeks) and its backend/frontend were built and rigorously tested to prevent claim errors; land rarity was confirmed to affect building aesthetics, diminishing XP boosts, and rarity-scaled maintenance requirements. (CC94, CC128, CC130, CC131, CC135, CC136, CC138, CC139)

items.name: Solace Land Grab Event (Live, Sept 2024)
items.desc: the event launched successfully: claim deed POA holders selected/favorited properties on the website map, live selection began Sept 24 and ran 5.5 days with a plot claimed roughly every 60 seconds; 7,680 of 8,000 Solace properties claimed (96%). Called a flawless launch with strong community turnout; claims could be anonymous or public (2,155 plots, 31%, chose anonymous). (CC141, CC142, CC144, CC145, CC147)

items.name: Land Ownership Flexibility
items.desc: land is not permanently locked to one plot: owners can disconnect and move/reclaim to a different zone as tech allows, and can relocate owned land between zones 1-3 instantly via database update (with seasonal restrictions); a maintenance-based system means players always keep their POA but can lose a specific location if maintenance isn't kept up, preventing abandoned claims from permanently locking map spots. Ownership itself is guaranteed safe for at least six months from claim. (CC129, CC130, CC141, CC142, CC154)

items.name: In-Game Claim Status Display
items.desc: every land plot displays a live claimed/unclaimed sign with a rarity-colored glow (white common → orange mythic), especially visible at night. (CC144)

items.name: Land Plot Building System Status
items.desc: building on land uses the same core system as apartments, but with prefab-style pieces rather than apartments' granular items; expected to open in the build following apartment release, timing dependent on rift combat progress and full apartment-bug resolution first. The 'Coming Home' release lets players build on paid apartments/plots with a storage chest system, expecting heavy IGC costs at the highest tiers. (CC124, CC140, CC145, CC148, CC151, CC156)

items.name: Solace Land Plot Fences (Technical Demo)
items.desc: temporary fences added around all Solace land plots as a technical proof that tens of thousands of objects can load instantly with no load screens; will later be replaced by player-built fences. (CC157)

items.name: Calido Valley Museum
items.desc: Scrapped --- a museum area with a customs-style checkpoint was planned for Calido Valley but was removed from the build per a developer walkthrough. Personal spaces remain planned for the same zone. (CC127)

items.name: Core Concept & Shape Evolution
items.desc: private, player-owned bubble worlds in five sizes like zone land, designed for a different use case than gameplay land (entrepreneurship, events, streaming, creation); persistent save state (remains as the owner left it), with saving/swapping multiple layout states investigated but not on the roadmap. All domes are circular (changed from an original rectangular design for better UE5 performance/aesthetics --- earlier rectangular dimensions are superseded), with the Copious (largest) dome confirmed at 380m diameter. (CC1, CC7, CC8, CC9, CC10, CC11, CC12, CC13, CC14, CC15, CC16, CC17, CC18, CC19, CC20, CC21, CC22, CC25, CC46)

items.name: Custom Dome Sizes
items.desc: Progressive Reveals --- sizes revealed in stages before settling on the final circular figures: medium at 120m×144m (2 football pitches), a largest size of 240m×200m, later an Epic dome at 336m×280m, with the top-end size left unfinalized for a while pending UE5 performance testing. (CC7, CC8, CC9, CC10, CC19)

items.name: Fair Play Algorithm (Anti-Bot)
items.desc: a proprietary anti-bot minting algorithm developed in-house, analyzing behavioral data to auto-cancel/refund flagged unfair orders; first deployed for the custom dome sale, described as early-stage but effective, and called their best and fairest sale yet. (CC22)

items.name: Custom Dome Sale Timeline
items.desc: a long prep runway (registration/verification, anti-bot test sales, marketplace/wallet testing) tied to timing around the Vasil hard fork; the sale itself ran Friday 26th-Sunday 28th, raising 4.23 million ADA, completing as part of Q3 2022 offerings. (CC6, CC16, CC17, CC18, CC19, CC20, CC21, CC36)

items.name: PvP Arena Domes
items.desc: owner-hosted combat/racing zones with invitable players, a laser gun weapon type, capture-the-flag as an example mode, turret/base-defense elements (needing balance passes, e.g. an overpowered turret), and monetizable PvP events; development footage shown ahead of a planned leak video. (CC1, CC14, CC15, CC17, CC20, CC21, CC38)

items.name: Racing
items.desc: Two Distinct Systems --- large-scale team-curated mega-dome racing (Calido Valley, 1M+ assets) is the primary competitive environment, distinct from smaller-scale custom-dome racing; the custom-dome version later confirmed as a racetrack builder letting owners pick an environment (e.g. Wild West) and build their own PvP track. (CC1, CC21, CC29, CC32)

items.name: Nightclub/Event/Concert Domes
items.desc: social spaces for concerts/festivals/live events with POA ticketing, proximity audio (louder near the stage), a stage screen for video, and support for comedy/keynotes; Seven's music tracks (community partnership) confirmed in the prototype; rebuilt from UE4 to UE5; EDM kit confirmed as a template. (CC1, CC7, CC10, CC14, CC20)

items.name: Live Artist Performance Partnerships
items.desc: Discontinued --- a separate, broader pursuit of live-performance/artist partnerships (beyond the Seven collaboration) --- including a second, unnamed music partner in early talks --- did not move forward. (CC7, CC10, CC14)

items.name: Custom Dome Templates (Launch Set)
items.desc: three initial templates shown at Vegas conferences: Art Gallery (for POA art/3D models, including Collector Club assets), Concert Venue, and PvP Dome; a Headquarters template followed for brands/influencers (Crypto Capital Ventures/Dan Gambardello confirmed first); three UE5 templates developed with a partial preview at Consensus. (CC12, CC15, CC20)

items.name: Cardano World
items.desc: a Disneyland-style gateway hub with sections for DeFi, metaverse, POAs, and gaming; individual Cardano projects get a presence with teleport access to their own domes, plus dedicated guild areas and a Cardano HQ; envisioned to extend into future themed worlds; confirmed pushed back on the roadmap but still planned; also identified as a potential virtual-conference venue (e.g. a CPOAcon replica for remote attendees). (CC14, CC15, CC26, CC27)

items.name: Cornucopias Collector Club
items.desc: a collab POA series with Cardano projects, bringing a 3D model of each partner's POA into the game as a placeable personal-bubble asset; community votes on future partners, with revenue share and COPI as the planned payment method; a dedicated 3D modeller was hired so this wouldn't distract from core dev. Jet Chickens (DripDropz/Kyle's project) confirmed as the first collab, shown live in a dome gallery. (CC19, CC20, CC21, CC22, CC23, CC24, CC25, CC26, CC28, CC35)

items.name: Crypto Bison Interoperability
items.desc: discussed with IOG's CTO at CPOAcon: a vision for cross-game POA usability (e.g. a Bison as a mount in Cornucopias), both games built on UE5; described as exploratory but positively received. (CC26)

items.name: Custom Dome Terraforming
items.desc: an early custom-dome build-system test let players terraform a water-only base into land and rocks while keeping playable water; the team later decided against that traditional height-map/voxel approach specifically for domes, opting for a different, faster/more performant method to be detailed in a future showcase. (CC12, CC21)

items.name: Building Tool Evolution
items.desc: moved from an MVP/templated launch kit toward a full drag-and-drop, zero-programming-knowledge builder; logic shared with the UE5 mobile game for a consistent cross-platform interface, and ultimately folded into the same unified apartment/land/dome builder system covered under Building & Property. (CC21, CC31, CC41, CC126, CC128, CC137, CC152, CC156)

items.name: VR Testing
items.desc: planned for when resources allow, using a small test group and leveraging the roles/permissions system already built for domes. (CC61)

items.name: Node Infrastructure Integration
items.desc: custom domes tied to server node infrastructure, letting node operators rent space to dome owners; development confirmed starting in January with a gradual, paced public release possibly landing later in the year. (CC1, CC146, CC147, CC149)

items.name: Advertising & Monetization
items.desc: dome owners can upload custom branding/images onto in-dome ad signage; pricing-sensitivity analysis underway for advertising credits; Calido Valley ad spaces already appearing, with some earmarked for future dome-owner B2B acquisition. (CC21, CC23, CC54)

items.name: Custom Domes Staking
items.desc: a land staking program pairing with custom dome POA holders, confirmed close to launch. (CC44)

items.name: Access Mechanic
items.desc: domes are standalone entities reached by direct flight, not a sky-plot-grab system --- a deliberate distinction from theme zone land plots. (CC54)

items.name: Native Token Support
items.desc: dome owners will be able to reward players with native Cardano tokens (possibly team-assisted token creation) for PvP prizes, event entry, loyalty programs, and competitions, subject to legal/KYC compliance. (CC10)

items.name: Building Kits via Marketplace
items.desc: kits previously bundled only with dome POAs are now separately purchasable through the Marketplace. (CC25)

items.name: World Map Placement
items.desc: domes appear as a distinct element on the world map alongside home bubbles and megadomes. (CC32)

items.name: Core Multiplayer Foundation
items.desc: the underlying replication/syncing/saving systems; core multiplayer confirmed working six months ahead of schedule (initially locally-hosted), with the team then shifting from building the foundation itself to building features on top of it. (CC22, CC136)

items.name: Global Connectivity & Scaling Tests
items.desc: a four-player cross-country test (England, Ireland, Sweden, Thailand) ran with no lag after a collision-mechanics overhaul; infrastructure then moved to cloud-hosted servers, targeting scaling toward 50-100+ players per session (up from an initial 3). (CC26, CC34, CC42)

items.name: Server Regions & Session Capacity
items.desc: players can choose between North America and Europe servers; sessions targeted at 100-200 players; Solace's sector count was revised down (~10 toward ~5 per zone) based on live performance testing. (CC1, CC7, CC9, CC10, CC32, CC44, CC67)

items.name: Monorail/Transportation Multiplayer Testing
items.desc: multiplayer replication (monorail sync, player positioning) tested during production; a critical two-player monorail bug found and fixed before air date. (CC51)

items.name: Voice Communication Systems
items.desc: Development spans spatial proximity chat that scales volume by distance and ties into world audio (e.g., nightclub music), VoIP/party channels that were delayed from Sunrise Social due to bugs like one-way hearing, and a long-term headset-based system targeted for 2026. (CC1, CC10, CC61, CC63, CC64, CC66, CC68, CC70, CC71, CC141)

items.name: In-Game Text Chat
items.desc: a text-based chat system built and tested internally, with profanity filtering needing further work; shipped as part of a live global chat system with a profanity filter in the Sunrise Social release, described as basic with more emoji/resizing/repositioning planned. (CC70, CC71)

items.name: Emote System
items.desc: a gesture/body-language emote wheel, first tested/teased then shipped in the Sunrise Social release; more emotes and wheel customization planned, some earnable through quests or purchasable bundles. (CC1, CC68, CC71)

items.name: Guild System
items.desc: a formal in-game guild structure with leaderboards, building on already-existing external guilds. (CC1, CC7)

items.name: District Model (Replacing Villages)
items.desc: the original whitepaper's 40-villages/36-houses model was replaced with a districts system, where each zone's land is organized into districts with a specialized utility focus (e.g. one district for mining, another for fishing); districts became the competitive/social unit. (CC1, CC3)

items.name: District & Village Competition Rewards
items.desc: district-vs-district and village-vs-village competitions with rewards, tied into governance and requiring decentralized voting systems; a district-level 'health/pie' score was added alongside individual character needs; a later refinement scores districts by their top ~100 property owners rather than requiring full occupancy. (CC1, CC38, CC142)

items.name: Guild Tools & Safety
items.desc: first-phase guild tools letting landowners delegate plot selection to another member without giving up wallet custody, plus a validation/vouching framework to keep guilds safe and legitimate. (CC85)

items.name: OG (Old Guard) Tier System
items.desc: a gated tier for early/dedicated supporters with annual exclusive POA drops, closed to new members between sales; a second knowledge/engagement-based tier was added below it; both require periodic re-verification/scrubbing (Discord activity checks) to keep the roles meaningful. (CC3, CC4, CC46, CC47, CC58)

items.name: Discord Points & Engagement System
items.desc: a daily-claim points bot ('Daily Corn'/'Gold Grab,' accessed via /daily) tied to future POA sale utility and raffle giveaways; later merged with a separate engagement-points system into one unified database-backed system (~90% complete) enabling future raffles, auctions, and sales. (CC52, CC54, CC83, CC114)

items.name: POA-Linked Discord Roles
items.desc: each POA type originally granted its own Discord role (e.g. Bubblejet owners); later simplified/removed for wallet privacy and security once the player account system could read wallet data directly. (CC1, CC52)

items.name: Random POA Giveaways
items.desc: gamified Discord giveaways separate from the points system, including one-off in-engine photography POAs of Solace/the racetrack at different times of day, each with its own rarity. (CC52, CC54)

items.name: Watch Parties & Community Events
items.desc: Discord watch parties with AMAs (a key new-player onboarding channel), weekly trivia nights, and community jetpack races/track events that double as server-scaling and mechanic tests. (CC1, CC24, CC114)

items.name: Community Contests
items.desc: an avatar celebrity-lookalike contest, a fan-art bounty (spaghetti-western poster), and a guild trailer contest (won by the KNS Guild). (CC2, CC89, CC105)

items.name: Community Content Channels & Library
items.desc: dedicated Discord channels for sharing avatars and apartment builds, retro-games chat, downloadable content (desktop backgrounds), and a broader public library of tagged gameplay footage/logos/fonts/music for community creators. (CC50, CC83, CC89, CC155)

items.name: Community City-Building Vision
items.desc: a proposed event where top community builders collectively construct a city within two weeks for Copi rewards, plus a proposed 'Learn-to-Earn Island' partnership with 10 universities' architecture/gaming students. (CC6, CC7)

items.name: In-Game Event Trophies
items.desc: requestable in-game trophies awarded to organizers of community events (Rumble Ball, apartment events), sized to event scale. (CC156)

items.name: Land Sale Role-Based Access
items.desc: the land sale opened in four sequential role-gated phases (OG group → POA holders → 30+ day Discord members → public), on supported wallets Nami/Jiro/Eternl, dated June 3rd-7th 2022. (CC6, CC7, CC9, CC10, CC11)

items.name: Land POA Rarities & Fixed Supply
items.desc: five rarities (Common-Mythic) all get the same plot size but determine testing/pick-order priority; fixed supply confirmed at 8,000 each for Solace/Esperanza/Fortune, no further minting once each zone's policy ID closes. (CC9, CC10, CC11, CC50, CC55)

items.name: The Great Land Grab Event
items.desc: five sequential rarity-ordered claiming events (Mythics first) with published 3D sector maps for advance scouting, coordinated guild/friend claiming, and 24-48 hour windows between tiers. (CC9, CC39, CC50)

items.name: Progressive POAs
items.desc: Cornucopias' dynamic-POA variant; land POAs are exchanged for these upon plot selection, encoding the specific location and evolving to reflect what's built on it. (CC50)

items.name: Land Sale Pricing
items.desc: approximately $200-$2,000 USD (revised down from an original $200-$5,000 estimate); exact ADA price left unfixed at announcement due to market volatility. (CC9, CC11)

items.name: Graphics & Hardware Settings
items.desc: adjustable graphics quality (useful before tournaments or on lower-spec hardware), and published PC hardware tiers (Minimum/Recommended/Best Experience), Windows-only at launch with Mac considered later. (CC46, CC48, CC49)

items.name: Cloud Gaming & Smart TV Access
items.desc: planned game streaming to Smart TVs and low-end devices with no graphics card needed, via browser or rented cloud PC, positioned as a way to lower the barrier to entry. (CC49)

items.name: Staged Testing Rollout
items.desc: pre-launch testing in phases: internal team → OG role holders → POA holders by rarity tier → public sign-up group, scaling toward 60,000+ potential testers; QA led by Chief Quality Officer Ant. (CC46, CC48, CC50)

items.name: QA & Bug Management Infrastructure
items.desc: a three-tier support pipeline (FreshDesk → Jira → dev team) with tickets linked to original sprint tasks, a global feature kill-switch for remote disabling, and planned security bounties for crypto-element testing. (CC48)

items.name: Player Roles & Permissions System
items.desc: an in-game role system (player/district/landowner roles gated by POAs, achievements, or level) letting the team remotely disable broken features instantly via a web portal; used to gate early launcher access by POA rarity tier. (CC49, CC50, CC57)

items.name: Friends System
items.desc: a friends list already in the desktop launcher, planned for full in-game integration; guild-sized group mechanics still being worked out. (CC1, CC10, CC12, CC67)

items.name: Community Content Sharing
items.desc: testers progressively enabled to record/share their own gameplay videos and screen captures, after initially holding back to build up quality content first. (CC64, CC69)

items.name: Matchmaking System
items.desc: for racing (and potentially rift battles), considering Epic Online Services or a custom build, supporting custom friend races. (CC1, CC29, CC40, CC42, CC47, CC50)

items.name: Sim Racing Wheel Support
items.desc: axis-mapping under discussion; since vehicles handle more like aircraft than standard cars, a limited (not full 900-degree) mapping is the likely approach. (CC29)

items.name: Holiday & Influencer Early Access
items.desc: a limited-time Christmas access gift for common/uncommon POA holders, and a separate early-access build for trusted influencers/content creators ahead of wider releases. (CC56, CC73)

items.name: Mainstream Early Access Onboarding
items.desc: 4,000+ early access applicants awaiting onboarding (tied to wallet/apartment readiness); a hotfix-triggered rollout planned to email 6,000 sign-ups with access codes and a free player-owned weapon. (CC152, CC155)

items.name: Vehicle Social Hangar
items.desc: a Star Wars-style social space to display/flex vehicle garages, with autopilot landing to avoid collisions and a vehicle-swap animation; may appear before becoming fully playable. (CC106)

items.name: Cornucopias Racing League (CRL)
items.desc: Core Structure --- a formal esports racing league with structured seasons, time attack/time trials, weekly events, and skill-tier matchmaking; racing confirmed as location-specific; three vehicle classes (A, B, C) running weekly qualifying heats → quarterfinals → semifinals → finals. (CC1, CC33, CC34, CC59)

items.name: Season X & Pre-Seasons
items.desc: Season X confirmed as the first official competitive season with a Class-S racing tier; informal 'Pre-Seasons' served as warmup periods before it. (CC1)

items.name: Esports League Outreach & Partnerships
items.desc: conversations begun with established esports leagues, plus Kop Ball outfit/prize competitions and a South American tournament partnership (a response received, planning conversation scheduled) as steps toward a full Esports Racing League. (CC93, CC99, CC117)

items.name: Racing Tournaments & Cups (General)
items.desc: small tournaments with Copi prizes rolling out before the full league; season cup confirmed (everyone-vs-everyone for the full season); partner/custom events planned for future seasons. (CC1, CC45, CC50)

items.name: Racing Game
items.desc: Early Public Demos --- first shown as a playable UE4 Javelin racing demo at Consensus (community competing for prizes), then publicly multiplayer-demoed at cPOAcon on a 4K/60fps screen (leaderboard, best time 2:25) with Charles Hoskinson and IOG staff playing live. (CC11, CC26, CC28)

items.name: UE4 → UE5 Engine Port
items.desc: the racing game fully migrated from UE4 to UE5 in about a month and a half (right after the custom dome sale), rebuilding systems broken by the new partitioning system and adding a new wheel physics system plus multiplayer support. (CC23, CC25)

items.name: Custom Racing Physics Module
items.desc: after prototyping with off-the-shelf assets, the team built their own physics module fully in-house, a process that took about nine months. (CC112)

items.name: Racing Game Physics Breakthrough
items.desc: a major physics breakthrough achieved after two weeks of work, enabling smooth, fast performance across multiple servers and countries. (CC33)

items.name: Racing Game Launch Timeline & Public Release
items.desc: The path to launch involved a long string of shifting estimates stretching from late Q1/early Q2 2023 through delays of "30-45 days" and "a few weeks," which progressed through internal team testing, an OG/POA-rarity-tiered rollout, and decentralized testing planned through Christmas; ultimately, the outer area of Calido Valley Raceway went live as Cornucopias' first true public-facing release, strategically timed near the T3 vehicle sale and OG mint to provide immediate racing utility for POA vehicle owners. (CC33, CC35, CC36, CC37, CC38, CC39, CC40, CC41, CC42, CC44, CC46, CC47, CC48, CC49, CC50, CC51, CC52, CC57, CC58)

items.name: Post-Launch Engine Upgrades (UE5.1 → 5.3)
items.desc: the team weighed staying on UE5.1 vs. upgrading to 5.2 for performance, then rebuilt again on UE5.3 for cloud release to testers. (CC62, CC69)

items.name: Racing MVP Modes
items.desc: practice mode, race mode (class-based leaderboards for OG Bubble Jet/Bubble Jet/Javelin), a fourth unrevealed mode, and a free-to-play test vehicle for non-POA holders. (CC34, CC42)

items.name: Racing Track Pit Stop Features
items.desc: Development includes a partially built physical pit-stop area for the Yellow track featuring spectator seating and team bays, though functional, Formula-1-style pit stops with crew mechanics for mid-race servicing were confirmed as excluded from the MVP and are planned for a post-launch update. (CC40, CC59)

items.name: Custom Friend Races
items.desc: considered for inclusion in MVP multiplayer as a lighter-weight racing option. (CC40)

items.name: Vehicle Class System
items.desc: a three/four-tier structure (A/B/C, later adding S-Class): A-Class (free T1, filled out with OG Bonanza and T3), B-Class (OG Bubblejet Sprinter, GTI Javelin, T1), C-Class (Bubblejet Sprinter, Core Dynamics Astro IV, T1). (CC1, CC57, CC58)

items.name: Performance Stat Testing
items.desc: real-world stopwatch-tested stats confirmed: Speed (top speed + afterburner), Handling (weight/maneuverability), Braking (aero brakes vs. reverse thrusters, vehicle-dependent), and Acceleration (0-1000m time trial). (CC1, CC57, CC58)

items.name: Vehicle-Specific UI/Dashboards
items.desc: each vehicle confirmed with a unique odometer/gauge design (OG Bubble Jet Sprinter, GTI Javelin, Bubble Jet, T1, T3 all shown). (CC42, CC47)

items.name: Core Dynamics Astro IV (Racing Context)
items.desc: new vehicle from in-universe manufacturer Core Dynamics, styled as a sporty courier with cargo doors, competing in C-Class. (CC57, CC58)

items.name: Valley Raceworx T3 (Racing Context)
items.desc: new A-Class vehicle ~20-30% larger than its earlier CPOAcon concept, multiple rarities with unique interior trims; mint completed via a one-per-person-limited 24-hour sale that opened additional tiers due to demand, introducing corn points during the mint. (CC57, CC58, CC59)

items.name: Yellow & Red Tracks
items.desc: Yellow (with bridges) and Red (tunneling, off-road sections) tracks revealed via leaked bird's-eye layouts, confirmed in active development. (CC59)

items.name: Yellow Track Rework
items.desc: the big loop section was completely ripped out and rebuilt after vehicles kept bottoming out/glitching, affecting G-force and lap times. (CC104, CC110)

items.name: Purple Track
items.desc: a new medium-difficulty track (Nürburgring-inspired with fantasy loops) sitting between Red and Yellow in difficulty, featuring cave sections, cloud jumps, and pump-fake turns; delivered to QA, tested live during a community watch party, lap times ~1:50-1:51. (CC101, CC103, CC104, CC105, CC109, CC115)

items.name: Wider Track for Shinobi
items.desc: a new, wider track built specifically to accommodate the faster Shinobi vehicle. (CC147)

items.name: Track Count & Difficulty Vision
items.desc: Calido Valley Raceway envisioned as a full racing park with multiple difficulty tiers; two tracks confirmed ready for testing with a longer-term plan for five to six tracks. (CC1, CC58)

items.name: Calido Valley Resort / Racing Megadome Entrance
items.desc: a themed walkable entrance area outside the Racing League megadome ('Taste of Solace') doubling as a Solace-mechanics testing ground: 17,548+ meshes/actors, 50+ brand identities, security robots, an air traffic control tower, a bubble jet showroom, AI-assisted info kiosks, night mode, regular monorail/lighting updates. Megadomes are dev-built (not sold to players) due to the heavy asset load needed for 800-900mph vehicles. (CC32, CC43, CC44, CC45, CC46, CC50, CC51)

items.name: Cornucopias Labs (Racing-Adjacent Testing Facility)
items.desc: a dedicated facility built into the Calido Valley entrance area for trialing new features (tree chopping, fishing, climbing, NPC interaction) before rollout to Solace. (CC50, CC51)

items.name: Environmental Tech (Calido Valley Walkthrough)
items.desc: realistic water fluid dynamics (footstep ripples, reflections, see-through clarity for fish), procedurally generated cave textures (real rock samples + proprietary materials), wind-reactive foliage/trees (UE5.1), and shared physics tech powering smoke and fire/campfire effects (fire still being finished). (CC53)

items.name: Racing Lobby, Kiosk & Pre-Race Flow
items.desc: confirmed sequence: enter Calido Valley → racing lobby → kiosk terminal (vehicle/track/outfit selection) → loading screen → matchmaking lobby (see other players' vehicles) → podium. (CC58, CC63, CC68)

items.name: Racing Lounges
items.desc: ~50 lounges around the track, hotel-elevator teleport access (random, with future VIP/OG selection planned), branded decor (e.g. Atmos manufacturer signage), ambient lighting/bubble jet effects. (CC60)

items.name: New Racing Start Point (Calido Pavilion)
items.desc: Calido Pavilion became the new race-starting location, replacing the original lounges. (CC74)

items.name: 16-Player Racing Lobbies
items.desc: scaled from early 4-player tests up to confirmed support for 16 racers on a single track simultaneously. (CC63, CC67, CC68)

items.name: Vehicle Collision & Damage
items.desc: physics-based collision with track walls/other vehicles; visible damage accumulates (dents, scratches) from racing and weather; no POA burning on crash; enough accumulated damage causes an explosion and removes the player from the race. (CC43, CC45, CC58)

items.name: Vehicle Repair, Fuel & Player Regeneration
items.desc: post-explosion, players are sent to an in-world 'medical center' (a regeneration concept, not a hard game-over); repairs use IGC or task-earned repair tickets; fuel required competitively (optional in practice mode), purchasable or task-earned. Explicitly confirmed none of this ships in v1. (CC58)

items.name: Vehicle Sponsorship & Wraps
items.desc: logo/sticker and full-wrap tech built into the vehicle mesh system; simple tier for general use, advanced custom wraps for major brand partnerships; Meld confirmed as the first brand wrap; guilds/teams/Cardano projects can brand their vehicles; player self-upload of custom wrap images planned. (CC39, CC45)

items.name: In-Game Racetrack Advertising (POA Ad Spots)
items.desc: POA-based ad spots sold around the track, shared impressions across co-buyers, early-adopter pricing, open to Cardano projects, other chains, and web2 companies. (CC45)

items.name: Vehicle Rental Platform
items.desc: a non-custodial system (POA stays in the owner's wallet) letting vehicle owners rent to other players for passive income; starts as a web browser tool before moving in-game. (CC47)

items.name: Dynamic POA Metadata for Racing
items.desc: an oracle-style workaround for Cardano's lack of native dynamic metadata support; race history/performance data written to chain and publicly searchable via API, enabling third-party esports leagues to build on top of it. (CC33, CC34)

items.name: Racing Leaderboards (MVP)
items.desc: time-trial leaderboards confirmed for MVP, starting simple with further development planned. (CC1, CC44)

items.name: Racing Data → Database Migration
items.desc: racing/vehicle data (times, history) moved from local saves to a central database to enable persistent leaderboards and tournament functionality; a lap-timing bug forced a leaderboard wipe/hotfix; long-term data planned to move to a DEGA-built Layer 2/3 for a public API. (CC81, CC85, CC87, CC91, CC97, CC98, CC99)

items.name: Racing Leaderboard UI/Design
items.desc: a first-draft leaderboard design (by Mark) shown pending approval, later shipped with a clean itemized layout (top 100+ racers recorded); noted as needing a UI overhaul once the page got busy. (CC92, CC98, CC150)

items.name: Bubble Jet Class-C Tournament
items.desc: an ongoing tournament with a 100,000 Copi total prize pool split across weeks, rotating a new featured vehicle weekly, with all weekly leaderboards combining into one giant leaderboard. (CC102)

items.name: COPIBoar Qualifying Tournament Series
items.desc: a leaderboard-driven tournament hosted by 'COPI Bore,' weekly qualifying events feeding into a final bracket round with prizes, possibly involving influencers. (CC98)

items.name: Arrow Trails Jetpack Racing Competition
items.desc: a jetpack racing competition across Kid Toledo and Solace 1/2/3 courses (Dec 2-15), individual leaderboards, cash-equivalent Rise token prizes (up to $250/course, $1,000 total). (CC146)

items.name: Arrow Trails Leaderboards (General)
items.desc: leaderboards for the Arrow Trails jetpack racing rings pushed through and released just before launch, enabling tournament tracking. (CC116)

items.name: Tournament Restructure
items.desc: a paused tournament rebuilt so sustained play over time increases finals chances, rather than rewarding one lucky run. (CC99)

items.name: Large Esports Group Tournament
items.desc: a large racing tournament partnered with an outside esports group, ready to launch once server-scaling issues resolve. (CC114)

items.name: Racing Matchmaking System
items.desc: multiplayer matchmaking requiring players to queue at a specific in-world location (GTA-Online-style); basic EC2-based matchmaking built first, with an ELO-style skill-ranking league system planned later. (CC29, CC56)

items.name: Controller & Sim Wheel Support
items.desc: controller triggers mapped to keyboard-equivalent keys (mouse/keyboard or controller supported) with in-game calibration menus; sim-racing-wheel axis-mapping discussed, though full 900-degree mapping isn't appropriate since vehicles handle more like aircraft than cars. (CC29, CC56)

items.name: Skill Tiers & Vehicle/Game Balancing
items.desc: skill-based tiers matching players of similar ability for special races and tier-based win achievements, alongside ongoing buff/nerf balancing based on player testing feedback. (CC29)

items.name: Racetrack Builder Tool
items.desc: an internal dev tool for laying out tracks quickly, first tested with simple placeholder shapes (triangles/circles) before applying to finished artwork, enabling scalable creation of the track ecosystem. (CC1, CC49)

items.name: Multiplayer Scaling Tests (Racing-Specific)
items.desc: internal demos scaled from 4 to 8 players across 8 countries on a hosted server ahead of public testing. (CC44)

items.name: Night Racing
items.desc: added as a byproduct of the day/night cycle: new lighting actors, emissive track lighting, billboard/structure lighting for night visibility, with performance optimizations so lights don't run unnecessarily during the day. (CC70, CC71)

items.name: V-Mode Camera
items.desc: a new in-race camera toggle (press 'V') that hides the vehicle model for a closer, first-person-style racing view. (CC80)

items.name: Racing XP System
items.desc: an XP algorithm tied to future seasons, awarding points based on racer count, finishing position, vehicle type, and racing suit worn. (CC70)

items.name: Racing Performance Optimization
items.desc: code optimized to support 8-10 simultaneous racers at high speed with minimal lag, even across long geographic distances. (CC99)

items.name: Vehicle & Environment Color Grading
items.desc: new color/saturation/tone adjustments applied to vehicles and Solace environments for better visual blending, with more tweaks expected. (CC80)

items.name: New Racing Game Music
items.desc: a community-requested track ('Game All Day') added via hotfix after the team noticed a community video edit using it. (CC89)

items.name: Custom Dome Racing
items.desc: a distinct, smaller-scale racing experience specific to Custom Domes, separate from the main Racing League; format not yet revealed. (CC1, CC21, CC29)

items.name: COPI Cross-Chain Listings & Exchange Expansion
items.desc: the COPI token expanded across exchanges and chains over time: Uniswap/ERC-20 (411+ holders), Gate.io, Bitmart, MEXC, LCX, Small Exchange, Min Swap and PancakeSwap (Cardano/BSC DEXs), MuesliSwap, plus a Binance-Cardano bridge to equalize pricing, ongoing ADA DEX liquidity provisioning, a fourth (BSC) staking pool, COPI token payment utility via the Collector's Club test sale, and Copi usable as Meld collateral/borrowing. Historical record of the COPI token's exchange presence prior to the November 2025 migration to RISE. (CC2, CC3, CC11, CC24, CC34, CC35, CC72, CC74, CC75, CC84, CC111)

items.name: COPI Stake Pools
items.desc: a set of Cardano SPO stake-pool offerings (the original ADA→ADA COPI pool, the 'Copic' pool paying a 125%-of-ADA-reward bonus, later raised to a 25% bonus over standard ADA staking) that let users earn COPI by staking ADA, with ~5.2M of a 15M COPI allocation distributed at last count.(CC99, CC114, CC115, CC116)

items.name: RISE Tokenomics Staking
items.desc: Per the official RISE Tokenomics paper (Nov 2025), staking rewards are now structured entirely differently, utilizing RISE and LP-token staking with a duration-based multiplier (up to 100 weeks) via Aerodrome/Minswap, meaning the fixed-bonus stake-pool mechanism no longer reflects how staking works. (T-Doc)

items.name: COPI Tokenomics Plan & Utility Rollout
items.desc: the original publicly-documented COPI tokenomics roadmap (developed with advisor Philip Black) describing gradual marketplace-utility expansion (moving toward all assets purchasable in COPI by end of year) and a sale-buyback mechanism (~20% split between liquidity and COPI purchases). Per the official RISE Tokenomics paper (Nov 2025), the reward-emission index, supply figures, and buyback/revenue-allocation structure were all restructured under RISE (e.g. daily emissions index changed from 2.5bps to 5bps of a smaller, reorganized pool; buybacks now follow a defined 100% P2P-fee / 30% premium-asset-revenue split) --- so the specific old plan and figures no longer apply. (CC4, CC14, CC19, CC24, CC31, CC42, CC45, CC47, CC85, CC86, CC88, CC106, CC107, CC108, CC110, CC113, CC115, CC119)

items.name: Migration to RISE
items.desc: the COPI-to-RISE transition: node operator/delegator rewards (previously accruing and claimable in COPI) confirmed to automatically switch to RISE, a 4-5 page migration document prepared and released, RISE claim availability discussed with Drip Drops, and a COPI Cardano native-token launch partner secured ahead of the eventual migration. Confirmed accurate by the official RISE Tokenomics paper: migration ran via ChainPort/VyFi starting November 13, 2025 at a 1:1 COPI-to-RISE conversion rate. (CC1, CC102, CC143, CC144, CC146, CC150)

items.name: Core IGC Mechanics
items.desc: earnable through gameplay (mining, farming, combat, quests, racing, etc.); used for everyday in-game transactions (ammo, small items, repairs, fuel); Copi token purchases IGC as a one-way relationship (IGC cannot convert back to Copi). (CC1)

items.name: Game Early Access Pass
items.desc: $10 credit card payment grants early access without needing a Cardano POA or crypto wallet; game will eventually be fully free to play. (CC1)

items.name: Corn Points System
items.desc: Evolution --- introduced during the T3 mint as a 24-hour minting-window mechanic well received across time zones; a free daily Discord claim channel let users accumulate points toward mint tier tickets; later merged with engagement points (liking/tweeting) into a single unified system, with corn points converting at a non-1:1 ratio.(CC58, CC59, CC112)

items.name: Machinations Economic Modeling Partnership
items.desc: financial modeling of the entire in-game economy to define currency flow and prevent exploits like money glitches. (CC62)

items.name: Cardano Testnet Economy Testing
items.desc: testing the in-game economy on Cardano testnet before full rollout, iterating gradually on real data rather than launching everything at once. (CC42)

items.name: Weapon Upgrades, Attachments & Skins Economy
items.desc: an IGC-based system for earning credits toward weapon attachments (scopes, magazines, stocks) that visually adopt the weapon's skin theme; premium/POA skin versions exist separately; accessories are craftable, vendor-purchasable, and retained when a weapon is sold/swapped; multiple in-world weapon manufacturer brands (Comoro Defense, Borne & Lee, Randos Metal Works) being built out. (CC121)

items.name: IGC-Purchasable Items (Non-POA)
items.desc: items obtainable with in-game currency alone, no web3 wallet needed: the Husky backpack (a grind, distributed via a dedicated vending machine or the Journey Shop/Corn Cuties store) and the SK47 battle rifle (lore-themed as pre-Calamity, refurbished by Old World Provisions). (CC122, CC139)

items.name: IGC Wipe for Upcoming Build
items.desc: in-game currency fully wiped for an upcoming build so everyone starts from zero, preventing exploits from unbalancing the economy; future wipes minimized but kept possible for exploit cases. (CC123)

items.name: Medal-to-COPI Melting System
items.desc: in-game actions (e.g. closing rifts) earn medals meltable into COPI via the store, creating direct token utility/demand; working title, still being finalized.(CC129)

items.name: Master Ledger for COPI Rewards
items.desc: a fully audited ledger tracking all Copi rewards from nodes and in-game earnings, feeding a rewards page/interface where players can view and move Copi to their wallet. (CC129)

items.name: Cornucopias Credits (CC)
items.desc: the standard off-chain in-game currency, earned through play (quests, trade, loot, activities), spent on everyday costs: repairs, crafting fees, travel, vendor purchases. (T-Doc)

items.name: Infinity Reward Points
items.desc: an off-chain reward-point currency earned by completing gameplay milestones/events across all modes (farming, racing, gathering, quests, crafting, exploration, building, mining, combat, fishing, and more); redeemable for marketplace discounts and determines a player's proportional share of the daily RISE reward pool. (T-Doc)

items.name: RISE Token
items.desc: the premium on-chain currency, purchased with real money, used for Cornucopias Credit Packs, cosmetics, seasonal content, and infrastructure services. (T-Doc)

items.name: Infinity Reward Eligibility Threshold
items.desc: qualifying for daily RISE reward-pool distributions requires maintaining a minimum 3,000 RISE balance in a connected player wallet (a dynamic, adjustable figure); framed as an anti-exploit safeguard, not pay-to-earn, since the RISE stays fully owned/accessible. Node operators' staking balance also counts toward this. (T-Doc)

items.name: Reward Multipliers
items.desc: players boost Infinity earnings via liquid RISE staking or a season pass (planned post-Season X), and via eligible POA collection/rarity multipliers; multiple methods stack. (T-Doc)

items.name: Asset Synthesizer
items.desc: converts eligible in-game items (rare/special/unique, earned via core gameplay) into fully-owned tradeable player assets via the dashboard; costs accumulated Infinity plus a small RISE fee. First confirmed example: the GTI Jester, an earnable one-of-a-kind X-Class racer. (T-Doc)

items.name: RISE Rewards on Every Marketplace Purchase
items.desc: every purchase earns RISE back to the rewards dashboard; paying in RISE earns a higher rate, other currencies still earn RISE at a reduced rate. (T-Doc)

items.name: Revenue Sources
items.desc: Marketplace --- generated via premium asset sales (fiat/crypto/RISE, though many premium items are RISE-only), Cornucopias Credit packs, node license sales, and four Season Passes per year. (T-Doc)

items.name: Peer-to-Peer Marketplace Fee
items.desc: a flat 5% fee on every player-to-player transaction, funneled to RISE burns and reward-pool replenishment (team-managed initially, moving to governance control). ((T-Doc)

items.name: Buyback Destination Framework
items.desc: repurchased RISE is allocated across reward-pool replenishment, liquidity provision, and treasury resources; community governance input on allocation planned as it matures. (T-Doc)

items.name: Buyback Activation Timeline
items.desc: the structured buyback framework activates upon Alpha release on Steam/Epic; the fiat/crypto/RISE payment mix determines buyback proportion. (T-Doc)

items.name: Migration Platforms & Mechanics
items.desc: COPI-to-RISE migration ran through two official platforms, ChainPort and VyFi, at a fixed 1:1 rate; official sites stay open through Dec 31, 2026. (T-Doc)

items.name: Migration Event Timeline
items.desc: COPI trading paused/DEX liquidity withdrawn at 15:00 UTC Nov 13, 2025; RISE went live on CEXs and DEXs (RISE/X pairs) one hour later; stake pools opened with boosted APRs simultaneously. (T-Doc)

items.name: Legacy COPI Pool Risk Warning
items.desc: LPs were warned to withdraw COPI liquidity before cutoff, since abandoned legacy pools risked bot arbitrage exploitation; legacy COPI pairs are now deprecated and don't reflect valid market value. (T-Doc)

items.name: RISE Total Supply Cap
items.desc: capped at 3,000,000,000 RISE, 840 million fewer than the original COPI supply. (T-Doc)

items.name: Community Rewards Restructuring
items.desc: the original 1.75B COPI Community Rewards pool was reduced and split under RISE into Community Rewards (724.1M) and a newly separated Node Rewards category (241.4M). (T-Doc)

items.name: Emissions Index Change
items.desc: the daily emissions index changed from 2.5bps (per the COPI Wiki) to 5bps of the smaller, restructured RISE pool, correcting an original play-to-earn model that was too front-loaded. (T-Doc)

items.name: Team/Advisor Allocation Reduction
items.desc: reduced from 921.6M to 821.6M tokens, keeping the team's percentage share within industry norms; the advisor portion was already fully vested/distributed by February 2024. (T-Doc)

items.name: Liquidity Allocation Increase
items.desc: increased by 49.6M to 164.6M, reserved exclusively for securing top-tier exchange listings (Bybit, OKX, Binance, Coinbase, Bitget, Upbit). (T-Doc)

label: Play to Earn / Play and Earn

items.name: Original Combined Launch Plan (Scrapped)
items.desc: play-to-earn was originally planned to launch alongside both the mobile game and main game together. (CC1)

items.name: Testnet-First Security Pivot (Replacing the Original Plan)
items.desc: the full in-game economy (coins, trading, exploit loopholes) is stress-tested on the Cardano testnet first, backed by a community security bounty incentivizing players and experienced Cardano developers to find exploits; play-to-earn would not go live until security was confirmed 'laser-tight.' (CC5, CC13)

items.name: Mobile Game Play-to-Earn
items.desc: Three-Phase Rollout --- Phase 1: a fully sound game with no play-to-earn; Phase 2: testnet API/economy integration; Phase 3: final live mainnet play-to-earn. (CC4, CC8)

items.name: Play-to-Earn API Development
items.desc: server-communication APIs for the mobile game built starting on testnet before moving to mainnet, as early-stage play-to-earn infrastructure. (CC15)

items.name: Mobile PTE Activation Trigger
items.desc: the play-to-earn segment turns on only after a 3-6 month testing/security period concludes. (CC13)

items.name: POA Utility & Multiplier in Mobile Game
items.desc: holding Bubble Jet or GTI POAs grants added benefits/multipliers at the end of mobile game levels, scaling with how many of the five Bubble Jets/Javelins are held. (CC4)

items.name: 'Play and Earn' Rebrand
items.desc: the team explicitly rebranded from 'play to earn' to 'play and earn,' keeping the same core reward structure (POAs, in-game currency, Copi) but tied strictly to active gameplay actions, not passive income; landowner staking rewards and community voting on reward mechanics confirmed as part of this model. (CC43)

items.name: Build-to-Earn
items.desc: Blueprints & Crafting Loop --- players design custom structures in the builder tool, convert designs into sellable/buyable blueprints, then gather required materials in theme zones to construct the actual structure themselves. (CC1, CC6, CC7)

items.name: Land Rewards
items.desc: Core Staking Mechanic --- land staking launched as an initial 3-month program paying Copi rewards, with land rarity affecting reward amount; stacking Ada-to-COPI-pool staking with land ownership produced a 'triple reward' (Ada from the pool, COPI for staking Ada, COPI for land ownership via DripDropz); confirmed as requiring active gameplay, not passive income. (CC1, CC11, CC15, CC16, CC17, CC19, CC20, CC21, CC23, CC43, CC44)

items.name: Land Owner Season & XP Progression System
items.desc: ~12-week seasons with landowners working toward ~100 levels via XP (building fences/farmyards/structures, players farming/harvesting on the owner's land); land rarity determines starting raw materials; future plans include an upgradeable farmhouse and tenant roles; rewards scale with level, paid in COPI; explicitly flagged by the team as subject to change. (CC57)

items.name: Vehicle POA Staking (Fuel Rewards)
items.desc: planned as a later staking phase after land/custom domes; rewards likely to be fuel or a similar in-game resource rather than Copi, since fuel is a required racing resource earnable via POA staking, in-game biofuel farming, or IGC/Copi purchase. (CC43, CC44)

items.name: Custom Dome & Theme Zone Land Staking
items.desc: a staking program planned to launch at the end of the first 3-month land staking program. (CC44)

items.name: Node Rewards (Core Mechanic)
items.desc: running a node earns Copi rewards over time. (CC1)

items.name: Node Reward Pool (First-Year Fixed Allocation)
items.desc: approximately 13 million fixed Copi tokens set aside for distribution across all active nodes in the first year, starting July 1st or sooner if licenses sold out and software was ready. (CC87)

items.name: COPI Stake Pool
items.desc: Growth & Mechanics --- the Cornucopias-run Cardano pool (ticker COPI, 5% fee, Ada never leaves the staker's wallet) grew from 311 delegates/2.84M Ada in its first week to 65M+ Ada at peak, with a declining reward curve favoring earliest stakers, a fourth (BSC) pool added for BSC-side holders, and eventual approach toward saturation before the COPI reward period ended. (CC18, CC19, CC20, CC21, CC22, CC23, CC24, CC25, CC28, CC30, CC31, CC44)

items.name: Grow Your Stake (GYS) Stake Pool
items.desc: a separate Cardano pool run by Josh, funding water wells across Africa, promoted as an alternative as the main COPI pool approached saturation. (CC31)

items.name: Portfolio Dashboard
items.desc: a dedicated web dashboard tracking POA staking rewards, stake pool performance, and overall POA portfolio, building on an existing partial node-rewards dashboard, planned for phased rollout into the main website. (CC23, CC29, CC30, CC31, CC33)

items.name: Gamified Community Education System
items.desc: gamified learning modules on Cornucopias/crypto security, earning badges that unlock Discord roles and future POA sale access; pivoted from a Discord bot to a web app for better UX; reached ~90% complete before being temporarily tabled to focus on the racing game launch, intended to be required before paid marketing began. (CC23, CC24, CC26, CC27, CC29, CC30, CC31, CC33, CC37, CC39, CC40, CC49)

items.name: AI Customer Support Assistant
items.desc: an AI model trained on the Wiki/internal design docs for a prompt/response support interface; a 'Lens' AI search feature was added to the Wiki (GitBook's built-in LLM) as a first step; appears stalled as of the most recent mention, with the Wiki not meaningfully updated since. (CC49, CC51, CC56)

items.name: Rewards & Progression / Economy System (MVP Draft)
items.desc: a simplified rewards/progression system drafted for the whole game, with Monte Carlo modeling planned via Machinations before a public announcement. (CC67)

items.name: In-Game Economy / Reward Structure Paper
items.desc: ongoing refinement of the economy/reward-structure paper ahead of community presentation. (CC70)

items.name: Leaderboard & Weekly Rewards System
items.desc: a live backend leaderboard (racing times, Holo Cache results) revealed at Consensus, enabling weekly competitions/rewards and described by the team as a turning point toward play-and-earn functionality. (CC93)

items.name: Market Economy Features (General)
items.desc: confirmed coming this year alongside apartments, land plots, crafting, and rift combat. (CC133)

items.name: Land XP / Land Leveling System
items.desc: a land-specific XP track separate from player XP; leveling land to level 100 grants 100% of season rewards (partial levels grant proportional rewards), tied to Season X. (CC135)

items.name: RP (Reward Points) System
items.desc: distinct from XP, rewarding activities like Rumble Ball, Hot Zones, and combat, potentially including in-game currency payouts. (CC140)

items.name: Land Rarity-Based Seasonal Rewards & Cosmetics
items.desc: land rarity determines seasonal reward pools, starting resource allocation, and cosmetic changes to building appearance. (CC141)

items.name: Quest Window, XP, IGC & Leveling Progression (Foundation)
items.desc: a quest-tracking window (completed quests, XP, IGC rewards, player leveling) built as the foundation of the quest system, with perk points and skill trees planned to follow; current progression flagged for a later wipe. (CC146)

items.name: Rise Rewards (Infinity Token)
items.desc: Early Version --- a system letting POA holders earn Infinity Token/XP from activities like Aero Trails leaderboard placement, later swappable for RISE cryptocurrency; templates/rules being built with the admin database team. This directly foreshadows the Infinity/RISE reward-pool mechanism later formalized in the official RISE Tokenomics paper. (CC149)

items.name: First In-Game Job (Burger Barn)
items.desc: the first job system, confirmed coming in the next release. (CC153)

items.name: Activity-Specific Skill/Perk Point System
items.desc: skills tied to the specific mini-game/activity played (delivery, Rumble Ball, Hot Zones, Arrow Trails, more to come) rather than freely tradeable across unrelated crafts; added quietly with no UI initially, tracking interface planned for a following build. (CC154)

items.name: Season Progression & Skill Trees (Shipped)
items.desc: Progression and Skills tabs let players earn seasonal XP and permanent skills via perk points, unlocking crafting benches and career paths, tightly integrated with questing and IGC earning. (CC155)

items.name: COPI Token Farming & Staking (BSC)
items.desc: after minting on Ethereum, the team ported to Binance Smart Chain for cheaper fees, enabling farming/staking for COPI holders. (CC1)

items.name: Two-Phase Land Sale Plan
items.desc: two back-to-back land sales confirmed: fixed-supply themed zones (1/2/3) first, followed shortly by the Custom Dome sale. (CC7)

items.name: Great Land Grab Events (Rarity-Tiered)
items.desc: five sequential land-selection events by POA rarity tier (Mythic first down to Common), with Mythic/Legendary holders also getting early alpha/beta platform access. (CC9)

items.name: Reward System / Leaderboards (Shared Foundation)
items.desc: a points/milestones/API-powered leaderboard system built for the racing game, designed to scale directly into the metaverse game as shared infrastructure. (CC39)

items.name: Skilled Gameplay Rewards
items.desc: Contribution Formula --- a player's reward share = their contribution over a time period ÷ the sum of all players' contributions for that period; this same formula underlies LP staking, RISE staking, node rewards, and skilled gameplay rewards alike. (T-Doc)

items.name: Infinity-Earning Activities (Full List)
items.desc: Infinity can be earned through digital real estate, farming, racing events, gathering, quests, crafting, exploration, building, mining, combat, fishing, and other gameplay --- explicitly not limited to that list. (T-Doc)

items.name: POA Multipliers on Infinity Earnings
items.desc: eligible POAs unlock rarity-based and collection-based multipliers that boost Infinity earned across activities, and additionally let holders claim free core resources (e.g. lumber) tied to the reward system. (T-Doc)

items.name: Reward Eligibility Framework
items.desc: Phase 1 vs. Phase 2 --- Phase 1 (testing through Alpha to Season X): all players earn Infinity for marketplace discounts/Asset Synthesizer use immediately. Phase 2 (Alpha to Beta and beyond): the reward structure evolves to a seasonal model with a season pass introducing exclusive content alongside reward-eligibility perks. (T-Doc)

items.name: Multi-Chain Marketplace (Cardano & Base)
items.desc: hybrid marketplace supporting both fiat and crypto/POA payments, with POA sales split evenly across Cardano and Base; player ID/profile system and cross-chain strategy both confirmed live. (CC1, CC48, CC49, CC51)

items.name: Fiat / Credit Card On-Ramp
items.desc: credit and debit card payments integrated for non-crypto users. (CC1)

items.name: Marketplace V2
items.desc: second version of the marketplace built alongside the desktop launcher and player admin system. (CC50)

items.name: Marketplace V3 (Multi-Chain)
items.desc: supporting Cardano, Base, COPI token payments, fixed-quantity rotating stock across chains, launched with the Quantum Autumn sale. (CC108)

items.name: New Marketplace System Redesign
items.desc: rebuilt to support wearable item components (hats, bodysuits, shoes), individual vs. bundled sales, and tokenomics-paper integration. (CC113)

items.name: Shopping Cart & Checkout System
items.desc: multi-item cart/checkout flow built to replace single-asset-only sales, iterated through several phase-3-sale releases before going fully live, allowing same-chain multi-item purchases in one transaction. (CC113, CC131, CC132, CC133, CC135, CC136, CC137, CC138)

items.name: New POA Marketplace (Website + In-Game)
items.desc: a new marketplace being built to exist both on the website and in-game. (CC122)

items.name: In-Launcher POA Marketplace
items.desc: desktop launcher planned to let players view/buy POAs directly before launching the game. (CC1)

items.name: Credit Card → COPI Conversion for POAs (Superseded)
items.desc: planned system to convert fiat card payments into COPI via DEX in the background to complete POA purchases. (CC108)

items.name: Fiat Onboarding via Infinity Wallet
items.desc: Per the RISE Tokenomics paper, fiat onboarding now flows through the Infinity Wallet system instead.

items.name: Anti-Fraud / Free-Item Exploit Mitigation
items.desc: systems reworked after spam accounts exploited a free-weapon giveaway, to protect future sales and tokenomics forecasting accuracy. (CC138)

items.name: Rise Token Exchange Listings
items.desc: RISE live and trading on CoinGecko, with CoinMarketCap and a Minswap/CoinGecko listing in progress. (CC145)

items.name: Vifi COPI Staking (Cardano)
items.desc: Cardano-native COPI staking via Vifi, one-month test then six-month program. Superseded by RISE's own duration-multiplier staking contracts. (CC44)

items.name: Native Token Support in Marketplace
items.desc: marketplace expanded to embed native Cardano tokens generally, not limited to COPI. (CC25)

items.name: Multi-Token POA Purchase Tech
items.desc: platform tech enabling purchases with COPI alongside ADA and other Cardano native tokens, tested via the bobblehead sale. (CC35)

items.name: Token Riot POA Marketplace Partnership
items.desc: Cornucopias joined the advisory board for Token Riot, a Drip Drops-built Cardano POA marketplace, and the platform later launched with a Discord competition and trading rewards. (CC66, CC79)

items.name: Secondary Marketplace (Anvil/WayUp Integration)
items.desc: API integration with Anvil's WayUp marketplace tech for buying/selling assets and land, branded seamlessly in-game; land holders prioritized first via the land app. (CC149, CC152, CC154)

items.name: Derp Birds Partnership (First POA Sale Tech)
items.desc: the very first POA sale (Bubble Jet Sprinter) used Derp Birds' marketplace technology. (CC36)

items.name: POA Tree Sale Series (VeriTree)
items.desc: a recurring charity POA line funding real-world tree planting (Senegal, Canada, and more), run across multiple mints on the team's custom Cardano minting platform, ultimately funding 100,000+ trees; also served as repeated stress-tests of the marketplace tech ahead of the land sale. (CC6, CC7, CC8, CC9, CC18, CC19, CC36)

items.name: Bobblehead POA Collector's Club Series
items.desc: the first collectible POA series (Farmer Joe and variants), bringing 3D partner-project models into the game and laying groundwork for cross-project interoperability. (CC34, CC35, CC36)

items.name: Bubble Jet Sprinter POA Sale (First Sale)
items.desc: the project's first-ever POA sale, held ~March 2022. (CC36)

items.name: Javelin POA Sale (Free Giveaway)
items.desc: the second POA sale hit major technical issues, resolved by giving away all Javelins free, making it the most widely distributed POA. (CC36)

items.name: OG Vehicle Mint & T3 Vehicle Sale
items.desc: sales filling out A-Class vehicle content, including a global-timezone-friendly tiered ticket system with free daily corn claims. (CC57, CC58)

items.name: Ethereum L2 Vehicle Sale (Valkyrie)
items.desc: a vehicle POA sale on an Ethereum Layer 2, payable via Metamask/USDT, expanding web3 audience reach. (CC69, CC75)

items.name: Weapon Sale Phases 1-3
items.desc: a multi-phase weapon/wearables sale line (Vanguard outfits, ballistic weapons, Superverse-branded items) rolling out across several builds, with some bundles delayed between phases for tech fixes. (CC120, CC123, CC124, CC130, CC131, CC132, CC133, CC134, CC135)

items.name: Apartment Sale (Hub City)
items.desc: the Hub City Apartments sale (Pinnacle/Elite tiers) went live, including five unique one-of-one giveaway apartments. (CC144)

items.name: Bundle Packages (Founder/Operator/Pathfinder/Pioneer/Citizen)
items.desc: a five-tier bundled asset sale offered to the community early at a discount before mainstream-gamer pricing at launch. (CC1, CC151, CC152)

items.name: Revolt Underground & Revolt Renegade Bundles
items.desc: store bundles (sniper rifle w/ scope, flamethrower, outfits) released and usable in-game. (CC157)

items.name: In-House POA Minting Technology
items.desc: custom-built (~$200k invested) eco-friendly minting platform, proven across 20+ live mint events, with fairness fixes (countdown timers, delayed batch distribution) added along the way. (CC2, CC4, CC8, CC11)

items.name: Land Sale Access Tiering
items.desc: phased website access (OG holders → POA holders → 30+ day Discord members → public) using POA-gated tech. (CC6)

items.name: Land Sale Queue System
items.desc: a queue-based sale flow letting buyers leave and get notified (email/Discord) when their turn arrives. (CC4)

items.name: Anti-Bot Measures & Marketplace Improvements
items.desc: backend/anti-bot upgrades made between the land sale and Custom Dome sale to reduce errors and bot activity. (CC16, CC17, CC18, CC19)

items.name: Rotating Fixed-Supply Marketplace Items
items.desc: items intentionally rotate in/out of the store with fixed, non-returning supply to keep the marketplace active. (CC112)

items.name: Corn Points Whitelist Tier (Juggernaut Sale)
items.desc: a 75,000+ corn-points threshold guaranteed early-tier (not guaranteed-mint) access for roughly 100 players. (CC112)

items.name: Player-to-Player Trading
items.desc: direct POA trading between players; supported by existing item pick-up/drop mechanics ahead of full in-game markets. (CC1, CC148)

items.name: Seasonal Asset Drops
items.desc: holiday/seasonal cosmetics made available in the store. (CC1, CC30)

items.name: Vehicle POA Scrapyard Mechanic
items.desc: fiat vehicle buyers reserve a studio-held POA; trading it in for a discount (instead of converting to a full POA) sends the reserved POA to the 'scrapyard' (effectively burned) --- an onboarding model for bringing traditional gamers into web3. (CC59)

items.name: Affiliate Linking Program
items.desc: content creators earn commission (e.g. 20% revenue) driving sales traffic via affiliate links; launched with a small group before wider rollout. (CC85, CC89)

items.name: Cosmetic Store Bundles
items.desc: avatar cosmetic bundles (hat, outfit, shoes, backpack, accessories) sold Fortnite-style, with POA ownership split into separate parts. (CC89)

items.name: Asset Lending / In-Ecosystem Marketplace
items.desc: players can grant temporary access (not ownership) to POAs like vehicles or tools for a set period while retaining wallet custody. (CC97, CC113)

items.name: Dynamic POA Game Item Stats
items.desc: POA-linked items can be buffed/nerfed over time via a cross-chain metadata-reference solution. (CC123)

items.name: Vending Machines
items.desc: in-game machines letting players purchase items directly as guaranteed loot acquisition. (CC130, CC140)

items.name: Nexus Express Terminal
items.desc: a branded terminal giving access to purchased premium assets (tools, weapons, avatar parts, clothing, backpacks), first located near the Cedo racing elevators. (CC109)

items.name: Skyland Real Estate System
items.desc: in-game real estate company letting players claim/purchase apartments with IGC or premium currency. (CC134)

items.name: Real Estate / Secondary Land Marketplace
items.desc: the land claim/viewing tool expanding into a full buy/sell/view real-estate marketplace via smart contracts and Anvil endpoints, plus a planned in-house first-party land marketplace. (CC142, CC152, CC154, CC155)

items.name: In-Game Brands
items.desc: the game already features 50-200+ of its own in-game brands, with the number expected to keep growing. (CC147)

items.name: In-Game Player Economy & AI Company Entities
items.desc: planned full in-game markets with AI-driven company entities (e.g. Bubble Jet) trading alongside players to help stabilize prices. (CC148)

items.name: In-Game Stock Trading
items.desc: planned feature letting players trade company stocks, tied to the broader dynamic economy system. (CC153)

items.name: Community-Voted POA Design & Sale
items.desc: community-submitted and voted POA design, minted/sold with proceeds potentially supporting wellness/charity/community causes. (CC41)

items.name: In-Game Screenshot POA Giveaways
items.desc: Unreal Engine screenshot POAs (Solace, racetrack at various times of day) with built-in rarity, given away as community engagement rewards. (CC54)

items.name: Bots Marketplace (Corn Points Redemption)
items.desc: a store letting community members redeem corn points for prizes. (CC83)

items.name: Holiday Node Sale (3-for-2)
items.desc: a limited 250-node holiday sale (buy-two-get-one-free) aimed at growing the active delegator/public pool operator base. (CC146)

items.name: Exclusive RISE-Only Items (Marketplace Roadmap Phase 2, ~Q1 2026)
items.desc: certain premium assets confirmed becoming exclusively purchasable with RISE, with a gradual transition toward the majority of assets being RISE-only as the player base matures past onboarding; accessibility remains the priority through beta. (T-Doc)

items.name: Smart Contract P2P Marketplace (Marketplace Roadmap Phase 3, ~Q2 2026)
items.desc: all items listed exclusively in RISE (no credit card or alternate currencies); seamless cross-chain trading between Base and Cardano via the Infinity Wallet; a flat 5% platform fee applies to every transaction. (T-Doc)

items.name: Automatic Wallet Creation (Infinity Wallets)
items.desc: Automatic wallet creation on sign-up using a behind-the-scenes abstracted wallet system with simplified authentication instead of seed phrases, finally branded as "Infinity Wallets" and entering testing as part of the final ascent to alpha. (CC1, CC113, CC152, CC154)

items.name: Epic Games Store Wallet Auto-Generation
items.desc: Auto-generation specifically for Epic Games Store entrants. (CC122)

items.name: Automatic Lace Wallet
items.desc: An automatic Lace wallet targeted for "the next couple of weeks." (CC151)

items.name: Player Accounts Launch
items.desc: player accounts launched as a foundational system supporting Calido Valley and future expansion. (CC64)

items.name: POA Role & Min-Spec Gated Launcher Access
items.desc: the launcher checks system specs against minimum requirements and detects POA holdings (Mythic vehicle/land) directly from the connected wallet to auto-grant download access, replacing manual role assignment. (CC67)

items.name: ChainPort Bridge
items.desc: Early Groundwork to Confirmed Migration Partner --- built as ChainPort's first Cardano integration linking the BEP-20 token to the new Cardano native token, delayed by the Vasil hard fork, later reused for the cross-chain ETH sale, and now confirmed in the RISE Tokenomics paper as one of two official platforms (with VyFi) used for the COPI-to-RISE migration. Same infrastructure, now load-bearing. (CC2, CC17, CC69)

items.name: Cross-Chain Wallet Support (General)
items.desc: additional Ethereum and Cardano wallets onboarded as part of the broader cross-chain strategy. (CC73)

items.name: Metamask/USDT Marketplace Payment Support
items.desc: Ethereum-based marketplace payments via Metamask/USDT, tested alongside the ETH node sale. (CC75)

items.name: Multisig Treasury Solution
items.desc: switched to a more efficient/secure multisig provider for treasury management, team payments, and fund movement. (CC86)

items.name: Base Blockchain Integration
items.desc: Confirmed Still Current --- Base (Coinbase's chain) added as a fourth supported chain alongside Cardano, Ethereum, and BNB Smart Chain, explicitly to reach mainstream players via Coinbase's user base. Confirmed still accurate: the RISE Tokenomics paper lists Base as one of RISE's native contract chains and one of the two initial DEX-liquidity chains (alongside Cardano). Not a pivot. (CC87)

items.name: Early Access Pass / Game Pass
items.desc: a $10 credit-card-purchasable pass letting newcomers play without a Cardano POA or Discord account, replacing the prior fully-gated web3 onboarding with a simple 'play' button. An early, simpler precursor to the fuller Infinity Wallet credit-card onboarding flow now specified in the tokenomics paper. (CC108)

items.name: Multi-Chain Marketplace Wallet Support (Cardano & Base)
items.desc: marketplace supporting both Metamask and Cardano wallets, reading/purchasing assets across both chains simultaneously. (CC110)

items.name: Nexus POA Recovery System
items.desc: a secure hub letting players always retrieve owned POA weapons/items even if lost in-game; POAs themselves are never wiped. (CC123)

items.name: Joint Wallet Development with Anvil
items.desc: Infinity Rising and Anvil jointly iterated on wallet technology, with future direction undetermined at the time; flagged for confirmation since the tokenomics paper specifies the Infinity Wallet runs on DFNS MPC architecture, not Anvil (Anvil separately appears as the WayUp marketplace/land-listing partner, so these may be two distinct partnerships rather than a contradiction). (CC149)

items.name: Copi-to-Rise Migration Bonus (Tiered)
items.desc: migration confirmed live and 1:1, with a decaying incentive structure: 5% bonus until Nov 23 16:00 UTC, dropping to 3% for 10 days, then 2% for 10 days before ending. Cross-checked against the tokenomics paper: the 1:1 conversion rate and Nov 13 migration start both match exactly; the specific tiered-bonus decay schedule is additional operational detail not spelled out in the paper itself, but it isn't contradicted by anything in it --- treated as accurate supplementary detail. (CC145)

items.name: Cardano Wallet Integration in Launcher
items.desc: the desktop launcher functions as a full Cardano wallet able to read the blockchain and display POAs; MVP allowed viewing only (not connecting), with full 3D interaction/creation planned later. (CC41)

items.name: Player Admin
items.desc: Wallet-Based Role System --- player admin system reading web3 wallets to determine POA ownership (land, domes, vehicles) for tiered testing access. (CC50)

items.name: Player Account System (Wallet Connect & Access Control)
items.desc: wallet connection, POA-based role/access assignment, and gated-access features built into a unified player account system. (CC52)

items.name: Credit Card Payment Rails
items.desc: Stripe, Apple Pay, and Google Pay all confirmed as accepted payment methods feeding into the Infinity Wallet purchase flow. (T-Doc)

items.name: New Wallet Integrations (Eternl/CC Vault, Jiro)
items.desc: two additional wallets confirmed working and included for the next POA mint and the land mint. (CC4, CC5)

items.name: Copi Token Governance (General)
items.desc: token holders vote on future game decisions. (CC1, CC15, CC17, CC23)

items.name: Community Governance via Cardano Token
items.desc: governance available to any native-token holder, enabling decentralized voting on game direction, tied to future Village vs. Village and guild systems. (CC1)

items.name: Guild/District Internal Voting
items.desc: decentralized voting for community groups. (CC1)

items.name: Community Naming/Governance Voting
items.desc: token holders voting on names for mountains, lakes, and areas as an early governance-practice utility, with final say retained by the team. (CC70)

items.name: DAO Planning
items.desc: planning underway for a DAO to gradually empower players/ecosystem through governance and voting. (CC128)

items.name: Governor / Town Governance System
items.desc: communities collectively vote on town improvements and tax rates within limited ranges, designed not to negatively impact other players. (CC129)

items.name: Community Governance for Reward Weighting
items.desc: planned voting on how rewards (nodes, play-to-earn, build-to-earn, POA staking, learn-to-earn) are weighted/distributed, following the initial land staking test. (CC17)

items.name: Dome Naming Governance/Profanity Filter
items.desc: custom dome naming rights restricted to POA owners, with a profanity filter and community-driven policing. (CC22)

items.name: Governance/Voting Tech for Copi Token (Pre-RISE)
items.desc: voting tech letting holders vote on staking rewards/fees ahead of expanded POA staking, cross-chain regardless of where tokens are held. Describes the pre-RISE governance model. (CC23)

items.name: Community Governance System (Wiki)
items.desc: a governance section added to the Wiki for community voting on in-game decisions, pending legal review. (CC5)

items.name: Cardano Governance Vote (K Parameter & Min Pool Fee)
items.desc: Cornucopias' community voted to support a Cardano Foundation proposal increasing the K parameter to 1000 and halving the minimum pool fee, for greater network decentralization. Unrelated to Cornucopias' own tokenomics --- a broader Cardano ecosystem vote. (CC52)

items.name: Voting Eligibility (Current)
