items.desc: governance credits accrue on all cross-chain RISE balances held in the player account (initially off-chain, transitioning to full on-chain voting as infrastructure matures); eligible sources are staked RISE, staked LP tokens (weighted by RISE share of the pool), and RISE held in the player account, even cross-chain. Unclaimed rewards and still-vesting tokens are explicitly ineligible. (T-Doc)

items.name: Voting Process (Current)
items.desc: proposals are created and managed by project representatives in coordination with the community, formatted as Yes/No or Multiple Choice polls; each includes a snapshot date (to prevent last-minute token swings), a linked discussion thread, and a defined end date, with results tallied and shared transparently. (T-Doc)

items.name: Advisory → Binding Governance Maturity Path
items.desc: votes are currently advisory/non-binding, with final implementation resting with the project team; the stated intent is to expand community voting's influence and gradually introduce binding mechanisms as governance matures. (T-Doc)

items.name: RISE Tokenomics Doc
items.desc: Community Q&A --- community questions from the released tokenomics doc to be answered, pending scheduling. (CC145)

items.name: Avatar Builder
items.desc: Technical Foundation & UE4→UE5 Rebuild --- the character system was fully rebuilt from an early UE4 pass into UE5 with heavy Nanite integration; Jim rebuilt the bone/mesh technical foundation while David handled the art pass (skin shaders, look, clothing behavior); A-pose used instead of T-pose to reduce animation deformation; faces made more human-like (closer to, but not, meta-scans); described by the team as the final generation of the character system ahead of launch. (CC1, CC10, CC15, CC17, CC20, CC23, CC29, CC52, CC58)

items.name: Avatar Creator
items.desc: Slider Count & Version Releases --- the creator shipped in successive major iterations: an initial ~100-slider release (down from an original ~300-slider ambition), a rebuilt ~64 body/128 face control version, then Avatar 3.0 with expanded definition/muscle sliders and better presets; each release pushed back slightly for balancing (original April 12 target slipped a few days) and was received as top-tier/AAA-quality by the community. (CC68, CC74, CC76, CC77, CC78, CC81, CC83, CC84, CC85, CC86, CC87, CC88, CC89, CC90, CC121, CC123, CC125, CC126, CC127, CC128, CC129, CC130, CC132, CC147)

items.name: Avatar Creator
items.desc: Feature Additions Roadmap --- planned/shipped additions across releases: beards and mustache/goatee variants, more hairstyles, hats, accessories, more complexion maps and underhair meshes, a randomize-all and section-specific randomize with per-slider lock, an undo (Ctrl-Z) for accidental randomize, symmetrize and naturalize buttons, and multi-preset avatar saving. (CC89, CC90, CC91, CC97, CC148)

items.name: New Character System (Testing Overhaul)
items.desc: a complete character-system overhaul entered testing builds, introducing some bugs/glitches the team worked through. (CC61)

items.name: Character Movement & Animation Overhaul
items.desc: a long-running thread of movement/animation improvements: new transitions, procedural animation/animation warping to fix foot sliding, elevator handling, multiplayer replication smoothness, and eventually a parkour-style landing roll after jumps/falls; iterated across many builds (Friday release, Sunshine build, Mythical Sunrise) before stabilizing. (CC63, CC65, CC66, CC67, CC134)

items.name: In-House Character Creator (UE5.3 Capability)
items.desc: UE5.3's mesh/bone improvements finally made an in-house character creator feasible, replacing prior Blender-based import workflows. (CC67)

items.name: Character Morphing System (Topology/Armature Blend)
items.desc: a system letting characters blend between body shapes (short/skinny to tall/large) while preserving deformation quality, functional after months of development. (CC17)

items.name: Procedural Runtime Animation System
items.desc: character animation calculated procedurally at runtime rather than pre-baked. (CC17)

items.name: Motion Matching & AI-Driven Animation (UE5.5)
items.desc: fluid, natural movement (including parkour) using AI-driven procedural animation and a ~600-animation database; paired with a purchased motion-capture suit to capture varied real human movement for realism. (CC117, CC118)

items.name: Character Creator Restrictions (Extreme Body Proportions)
items.desc: height ranges and adjustable toe/hand length restricted to fix animation and equipment bugs (e.g. hats clipping through jetpack bubbles) caused by extreme proportions. (CC117)

items.name: Hair System (Nanite/Skeletal Hybrid)
items.desc: Nanite hair for shorter/male styles combined with skeletal mesh for longer styles (e.g. ponytails) to allow proper animation; expanded hairstyle roster (bald, mullet, faux hawks with curliness/texture variants, buzz cut, ponytail, bobs) modeled in Blender for import. (CC86, CC97, CC120, CC127)

items.name: Body Art / Pigment & Tattoo System
items.desc: a lore-based 'Quantum Pigment Manipulator' lets players apply tattoos/stickers/face paint and change skin/body color (Hulk-style); later removed from slider-based customization and planned to return as an in-world 'varnish shop'/tattoo-parlor-style system for a more lore-friendly implementation. (CC86, CC89, CC132, CC147)

items.name: Character Needs System
items.desc: survival stats (hunger, thirst, tiredness, heart rate, blood level, energy, calories) affected by environmental temperature/humidity and running; different zone climates affect the system; built by Technical Director Jim as a core driver of the in-game economy. (CC1, CC17, CC22, CC38)

items.name: Pre-Selected Test Characters (Lauren, Penny, Mythic Mike, Seth, Michelle)
items.desc: ready-made characters for early public testing before full customization was ready, later becoming interactive background NPCs. (CC52)

items.name: Avatar Creator Celebrity/Community Contests
items.desc: a recurring contest format: players recreate celebrities or compete cross-community (Superverse, Neotokyo) with Twitter community voting, prizes in Copi/POAs/free access, timing repeatedly shifted to align with other releases (apartment sale, market conditions). (CC88, CC90, CC91, CC133, CC135, CC140, CC147)

items.name: Rob & Josh Bobblehead Avatar Community Event
items.desc: planned official Rob/Josh avatars for the community to remix into bobblehead-style fan versions using the Avatar Builder. (CC6)

items.name: Outfit System
items.desc: Core Mechanics --- premium, earnable, and seasonal outfits confirmed to carry real gameplay traits/stats, not just cosmetics (e.g. a bulky suit trading fall survivability for trip/sweat chance, a hazmat suit resisting environmental hazards); outfits also grant situational XP bonuses tied to the activity performed. (CC1, CC23, CC33, CC52, CC89)

items.name: Outfit-Switching During Racing
items.desc: requires additional menu programming so players can select a race-appropriate outfit instead of racing in whatever they're currently wearing; not available in early racing test iterations. (CC58)

items.name: Armor Tiers (Light/Medium/Heavy)
items.desc: heavier armor slows movement, letting players choose a rogue/light vs. tank/heavy playstyle. (CC1)

items.name: Material/Texture Card (Mat Card) System
items.desc: swappable material cards (leather, chrome, fabric, etc.) let players mix one outfit's geometry with another's materials; every premium outfit purchase includes a collectible Mat Card (database-tracked, not an POA) swappable across interchangeable outfits; a crafting/exchange mechanic for trading cards was under consideration. (CC1, CC97, CC109, CC121)

items.name: World Breaker Starting Suit
items.desc: the lore-tied starting outfit (players arrive as refugees from the 'World Breaker' with nothing), later redesigned based on player feedback. (CC82, CC120)

items.name: Cheeky Krypto Race Suit
items.desc: a limited-edition racing suit/helmet developed over a year in partnership with Cheeky Krypto, shipping as a wearable in-game item (not just a PFP), with utility granting holders access to Cheeky Crypto seed rounds/early sales; later needed splitting into three separate items (helmet/suit/shoes) for Nexus compatibility. (CC1, CC23, CC33, CC36, CC68, CC136)

items.name: Vanguard Outfit Line
items.desc: men's/women's Vanguard Premium Apparel Sets (hat, outfit, shoe) and a separate Vanguard Scouts outfit, sold with a materials/color pack for recoloring. (CC106, CC109, CC110)

items.name: Cyber Suits (Light/Medium Armor Starting Gear)
items.desc: new starting-tier armor outfits, requiring rework after body-proportion changes elsewhere in the avatar system. (CC126)

items.name: MOP Suit (Mobile Operations Protection Platform)
items.desc: a legendary trooper-style outfit by Core Dynamics, included in every Operator bundle purchase (male/female versions). (CC153)

items.name: Additional Named Outfits
items.desc: Mining Outfits (multiple variants: jackets, tank tops, helmets, boots), a casual feminine-presenting outfit, Fishing and Racing utility outfits, and the Light Armor Adventure premium skin. (CC97, CC102)

items.name: Heavy & Medium Armor Sets (IP-Defining Design)
items.desc: armor sets designed for iconic, franchise-defining looks (compared to Halo/Star Wars), not expected ready for immediate sale. (CC145)

items.name: Cosmetic Perks Documentation
items.desc: a planned document detailing in-game traits/perks (e.g. damage mitigation) tied to specific cosmetic gear like the Vanguard line. (CC107)

items.name: Corn Cuties Brand
items.desc: a dedicated cute-aesthetic cosmetic line (backpacks, charms, accessories) designed by team member Katherine. (CC1, CC109)

items.name: Hat & Bling Accessories
items.desc: general cosmetic accessories sold in-store. (CC1)

items.name: Backpack Cosmetics (General & Named)
items.desc: visible backpacks providing inventory storage; named releases include Titan XL, Blackhorn Tactical Outlander, Corn Cuties variants (Grizzly Purple Fury, Brown Brawler, Prowler, Blush Bandit, Husky), Luna Deluso (including a mythic 24-karat gold pearl version), and the Rugged M hard-shell backpack. (CC1, CC106, CC109, CC122, CC153)

items.name: Jetpack Cosmetics (Named)
items.desc: themed jetpack skins matching outfit lines: Zero-G Stratos (quantum-compression propellant regen, ~8 storage slots), Randos Junker (surface-faction lore), Cloud Angels animated jetpacks, and the Corn Cuties monkey jetpack. (CC1, CC109, CC156)

items.name: Helmet Cosmetics
items.desc: seasonal/themed helmets including the Quantum Jack pumpkin/Halloween helmet (free giveaway, animated flame effects, gas-fee-only). (CC1, CC109)

items.name: POA Items With Future Utility
items.desc: cosmetic items hinted to gain gameplay utility over time, e.g. a Burger Barn hat potentially granting discounts/perks at Burger Barn. (CC1)

items.name: Player Identity Tags
items.desc: a custom, searchable gamer-tag system replacing default hashtag+number IDs, attachable to vehicles/land/domes; launching non-POA before becoming a player-owned asset later. (CC78)

items.name: Inventory & Equipment System (Avatar-Linked)
items.desc: a leaked inventory/equipment screen (outfit, accessory, clothing, food, tools sections, backpack slots, avatar equip slots, XP tracking); later confirmed being built in sync with the Character Creator. (CC75, CC111)

items.name: First-Person View
items.desc: planned for vehicle interiors and potentially free-roam. (CC1)

items.name: Emote / Gesture System
items.desc: a full emote wheel and animation set, shipping with 10 emotes (dance plus nine others) accessible via the B button. (CC1, CC70)

items.name: In-Game Avatar Equip System
items.desc: updated system letting players equip items directly onto their avatar in-game. (CC110)

items.name: Shoes (First Apparel Category)
items.desc: shoes introduced as the marketplace's first apparel item type (including mythic variants); the Comet Shoes became the first item usable in-game immediately upon purchase. (CC139, CC141)

items.name: New Playable Character 'Cole'
items.desc: a new character inspired by 'Nikki,' featuring an Indiana-Jones-style hat and wind-reactive elements. (CC70)

items.name: Luna Deluso Fashion Brand
items.desc: a high-end in-world fashion shop (Cleo Pavilion) selling designer backpacks. (CC74)

items.name: Vehicle Light Kits & Sponsorship Wraps
items.desc: cosmetic light kits for flying vehicles (Bubble Jet/Javelin compatible, 8,000 supply) and logo/sticker wrap tech for sponsorships, laying groundwork for full team/guild/brand wrap customization. (CC34, CC39)

items.name: Avatar Skin Tone Testing
items.desc: early internal testing of avatar skin colors (e.g. blue), ahead of a planned character-creation deep-dive video. (CC29)

items.name: Character Creator in Racing Entrance
items.desc: Character Creator made available in the Racing League entrance area with default options, giving early hands-on access before full Solace launch. (CC43)

items.name: Core NPC Vision (Founding Statement)
items.desc: AI-powered NPCs trained on their specific in-game role via AI agents; conversational NPCs players can walk up to and talk with, responding based on role/knowledge; a future vision where AI-powered NPCs can themselves be owned as POAs; NPC farm helpers players can own to assist with farming tasks; NPC quest givers stationed in towns and areas, with Civic Works terminals serving as quest interaction points. (CC1, CC13)

items.name: NPC Crowd & Ambient Life System
items.desc: AI-driven pedestrian NPCs to bring towns and sector hubs to life, from an early prototype shown in build previews, through an internally-built crowd-preset system waiting on the Avatar system to finish, crowd elements hinted in the Juggernaut sale video, and finally first real crowd-testing deployed in the Eclipse nightclub --- working well and popular with players, though feedback requested more music tracks. (CC1, CC78, CC113, CC156)

items.name: New NPCs
items.desc: Calido Magic Hour Update --- additional NPCs added as part of the Friday Calido Magic Hour release. (CC65)

items.name: Tess (T55) Robot Tour Guide NPC
items.desc: a robot NPC built as an onboarding tour guide with a full set of voice lines and jokes; voice lines were turned off in a recent build due to a packaging error, though the functionality itself works fine internally. (CC66)

items.name: NPC/Animal AI & Navigation
items.desc: non-LLM AI navigation and decision-making (animals fleeing players, NPCs choosing targets) in active development toward combat. (CC109)

items.name: AI Wiki Summaries
items.desc: AI-generated summaries added to the Wiki, separate from in-game NPC work. (CC115)

items.name: AI-Powered NPCs
items.desc: LLM Research & Model Testing --- active research into LLM-driven NPCs with unique personalities trained on Cornucopias lore, including Nvidia's ACE program; about a dozen LLM models tested (Grok, Llama 3.2, a Chinese model, and others) narrowed to four, with a working NPC prototype already giving out quests; partnerships explored with SingularityNET, Sophia Verse, and DMA; an in-house player-NPC interaction plugin, voice-to-text-to-voice, and facial animation layers all under exploration; POA ownership of AI agents floated as a future extension. (CC116, CC117, CC118)

items.name: Facial Capture / Talking NPC Tech
items.desc: facial capture capability enabling characters to talk, part of ongoing R&D toward more lifelike NPCs; research-stage, not confirmed for the immediate next release. (CC120)

items.name: LLM-Based NPC Communication Test
items.desc: an early test communicating with a downloaded LLM, described as working nicely with more steps to go. (CC120)

items.name: Wandering NPC AI (First-Iteration Movement)
items.desc: a first-pass AI NPC shown moving/walking the world in small, unpatterned steps, an early step toward NPCs that will eventually give quests and fight. (CC120)

items.name: AI-Generated Real Estate Agent ('The Reserve')
items.desc: an AI-created real estate agent character and commercials for the in-game apartment brand, with more AI-driven marketing content planned. (CC144)

items.name: AI-Driven Industry Economy Actors
items.desc: major industry NPCs (e.g. Jet, parent of Bubble Jet; steel manufacturers) trading in bulk with players, forming a full economy from micro plot-level trading to macro cross-zone trade with taxes and middlemen; planned as a major focus the following year. (CC145)

items.name: AI-Powered NPC Agents (Robots/Pets/Workers)
items.desc: gradual development of mini-LLM-driven NPC agents that could take the form of robots, pets, companions, or workers (maids/butlers). (CC147)

items.name: Emma NPC Guide & Intro Cinematics
items.desc: a Cornucopias government NPC guide voiced over radio, touring and explaining the game to new players via redone cinematics, with a planned 'part two.' (CC148)

items.name: AI Follower Avatar (Companion)
items.desc: a planned dumb AI-controlled follower version of a player's secondary saved avatar, able to accompany them in-world. (CC148)

items.name: AI Companion with LLM Memory & Voice Synthesis
items.desc: a premium companion feature that remembers shared experiences with the player, talks via voice synthesis, and gives contextual advice (e.g. referencing past rift battles); being built in incremental MVP steps. (CC148)

items.name: Security Drones
items.desc: bounty-system enforcement drones found/added in Solace; unclear if they'd make the immediate next build but confirmed coming. (CC150)

items.name: AI-Generated Voiceovers (Placeholder)
items.desc: AI-generated voiceovers/loading-screen audio used as placeholders while quest scripts are finalized, to be replaced by human voice actors once content is locked. (CC150)

items.name: AI-Powered NPCs
items.desc: LLM Integration (Sellable Asset) --- an LLM integrated into Unreal Engine and working in staging, letting players communicate with bots; planned to sell as player-owned asset bundles delivered in phases over 6 months to a year. (CC156)

items.name: AI Companion Drones (Alita, Aeron, Kiko, Clanker)
items.desc: named companion drones with emotional-matrix systems reacting to player interaction; sale launched, core tech mostly complete with individual features still being implemented. (CC157)

items.name: NPC Character 'Carl'
items.desc: a named NPC shown driving the GTI Javelin at high speed; full name still being finalized. (CC1)

items.name: Character Needs System (Maslow's Hierarchy / Wheel of Life)
items.desc: a ~9-month effort incorporating Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, the Wheel of Life coaching framework, and the Octalysis gamification framework to score character wellness (financial, community, work, etc.) and tie it to reward pacing. (CC38)

items.name: AI Customer Support Model
items.desc: an AI model (possibly ChatGPT/Stability AI-based) planned for training on the Wiki and game design docs to power a web-based support tool. Appears elsewhere in this document as stalled by later episodes --- worth reconciling status during the full audit. (CC49)

items.name: AI-Powered Information Kiosks
items.desc: Calido Valley info kiosks wired to an AI/LLM backend trained on the Cornucopias wiki to answer player questions. (CC51)

items.name: Copi Wiki AI ('Lens') Integration
items.desc: an AI search feature integrated into the Wiki via GitBook, letting users ask questions and get answers plus source links, trained only on wiki data; described as a major Q2 addition. (CC56, CC57)

items.name: Desktop Launcher
items.desc: Core Development & Milestones --- a long-running centerpiece: a secure game launcher with tamper checks, bug submission, and update viewing, reported repeatedly as nearing completion (99%) with a small public test group planned 'within a week'; functionality-complete internally while UI/design was refined; a major later overhaul added inpoint caching for performance, update-pending notifications, an error page, extensive debug logging, choice of install location, move/remove options, file-verification UI, and repackaging via the 'Squirrel' system for automatic updates (download time cut to ~15 minutes); by CC61, community tester Scruffy was using it to create a player account and launch the game itself --- the first time launcher, game, and player accounts all worked together live. (CC1, CC10, CC11, CC33, CC41, CC49, CC53, CC54, CC56, CC58, CC61, CC67)

items.name: Desktop Launcher Rewrite (Jeff & Matt)
items.desc: the launcher rewritten from scratch by a new team: a redesigned login screen connected via web API to the website/wallet, a patch notes screen, a 'my game assets' POA section, and a profile section with PFPs. (CC43)

items.name: Desktop Launcher Redesign (Mark)
items.desc: the original launcher's designer set to lead a bigger redesign once website work progressed far enough. (CC31)

items.name: Launcher POA/Hardware Detection Update
items.desc: launcher updated to detect a player's graphics card/system specs and recognize owned POAs (Mythic, Legendary, etc.), enabling tiered content delivery to different tester groups. (CC64)

items.name: Launcher-Based Testing Access Rollout
items.desc: testing access expanded to 170 OG testers, with the launcher itself set to coordinate the next access wave by role, POA ownership, and hardware (Mythic Zone, racing vehicle, and Custom Dome holders next). (CC65)

items.name: Launcher News Feed
items.desc: a news section built into the launcher to keep players game-focused, confirmed essential and included even in a scaled-down MVP form. (CC41)

items.name: Test Game Launcher (Internal QA Tool)
items.desc: an internal-only launcher variant pulling daily QA build files via the node network; not yet production-facing, but download-time optimizations from it were significant. (CC112)

items.name: Player Account System
items.desc: Launch & Growth --- a secure account system (username/password, Discord + web3 wallet linking, 2FA, profile picture, POA asset viewing) launched to OGs first then the public on cornucopia.org; grew past 900 accounts within a day and over 2,000 shortly after; security rating improved from an F to an A++ following testing; later confirmed live with working player roles via the player portal website. (CC51, CC53, CC54, CC55, CC57)

items.name: Player Account UI Performance Improvements
items.desc: lazy loading and a toggle to disable video previews added after OG tester feedback, improving scroll performance for wallets holding many POAs. (CC54)

items.name: Username Profanity Filter
items.desc: a multilingual filter actively refined after testing revealed false positives blocking innocuous words in other languages, balancing family-safety with fairness. (CC54)

items.name: Testing Group Signup & Player Profile Setup
items.desc: sign-ups opened via the website for a testing group, including setting up player profiles ahead of full launcher/account testing. (CC49)

items.name: Website Redesign
items.desc: Ongoing Multi-Year Effort --- a full site rebuild pursued across many episodes: a new React developer brought on, an MVP staged for internal QA before public launch, a fully custom-coded site with login/admin access and a centralized management console added, supporting a rewards/POA dashboard and the Copious Academy module; ultimately delivered by Jeff with real functionality well beyond the original site, in support of the player account and launcher rollout. (CC23, CC29, CC31, CC33, CC34, CC36, CC37, CC39, CC44, CC54)

items.name: Vehicle Gallery Page (Website)
items.desc: a dedicated vehicle showcase page for the redesigned website, letting users click through to see colors/stats; shown as a work-in-progress leak with placeholder data. (CC37)

items.name: New Cornucopias Logo
items.desc: updated to a cleaner white version with the old 'Island of Weights' imagery removed, rolled out across the website and launcher. (CC43)

items.name: Portfolio / Rewards & POA Holdings Dashboard
items.desc: a dashboard built to show staking rewards, POA staking status, and overall portfolio performance, including single sign-on. (CC23, CC33)

items.name: Load-In / Character Select Screen
items.desc: a pre-game menu with genuine 3D depth (not a flat image), showing wallet/store/inventory/quest tabs and feeding directly into character selection; also shown separately as a completed in-game 3D menu ready for public testing. (CC52)

items.name: In-Game Menu Build (Dean & Declan)
items.desc: the full in-game menu system, reported 60-70% complete before reaching full completion, with controller support (mouse/keyboard/controller) integrated; design philosophy kept menus simple, clean, and context-specific (e.g. only fishing-related UI while fishing), overseen by Jeff and implemented by Michael. (CC55, CC62)

items.name: Compass Navigation Tool
items.desc: a top-of-screen compass introduced alongside the holocache system, confirmed as core navigational functionality carrying into Solace. (CC62)

items.name: Inventory System
items.desc: a jigsaw-puzzle-style drag-and-drop inventory (backpack/chest/vehicle storage slots, controller support, bulk item dropping) shipped as a core Solace-readiness system, later reappearing as the 'Nexus' inventory system in a major build, with continued updates tested alongside other components. (CC63, CC81, CC110, CC127)

items.name: Nexus Terminal
items.desc: an in-game terminal letting players transfer purchased marketplace assets from their wallet into their in-game inventory. (CC111)

items.name: Overhauled Game UI (General)
items.desc: the entire UI confirmed completely redesigned compared to the prior year, alongside the addition of multiplayer racing. (CC68)

items.name: Gamma Slider
items.desc: a brightness/contrast adjustment slider, not yet implemented but confirmed planned to help with monitor display issues. (CC78)

items.name: Improved Graphical Menu/Options
items.desc: an improved graphics options menu added for better performance control. (CC109)

items.name: Real-Time Menu
items.desc: a new real-time menu added as part of ongoing UI updates and graphics optimizations tested with the community. (CC111)

items.name: Main Menu Visual Update
items.desc: new coloring and background elements applied to the main menu, with screenshot updates still pending. (CC126)

items.name: Updated Graphics Settings Tiers
items.desc: all graphics presets (Ultra, High, Medium) recalibrated upward for next-gen GPUs, meaning returning players need to step down a setting level from what they previously used. (CC132)

items.name: Menu System Facelift & Combat Wheel
items.desc: all menus received a visual facelift, including a new combat radial wheel with slots reserved for future tools/food items. (CC132)

items.name: Interaction Indicators
items.desc: new UI markers added for actionable objects (loot boxes, Nexus terminals, store terminals, credit machines) to improve player onboarding clarity. (CC139)

items.name: Game Access Waitlist / Gating
items.desc: new sign-ups gated into a waitlist ahead of Steam/Epic traffic, to control access gradually as the game approaches mainstream launch. (CC145)

items.name: Mobile Game UI
items.desc: early mobile game UI designs begun, styled to closely match the PC game's interface. (CC4)

items.name: Unified UI/UX Design (Cross-Platform)
items.desc: a consistent look and feel designed for the mobile game's interface, intended to later extend to the desktop launcher, main game, and eventually the main website. (CC5)

items.name: Badges Feature (Gamification)
items.desc: a new badges system confirmed in development, described as an important feature with more details to follow. (CC13)

items.name: Epic Games Store & Steam
items.desc: early wishlist-page ambitions grew into a confirmed three-stage rollout (waitlist listing with trailer → soft launch tied to a following build → marketed hard launch/alpha), with trailer production iterating toward increasingly real in-engine and eventually actual game footage; Steam passed identity verification and page review; both platforms went live as "coming soon" with wishlist funnels running, then fully listed, with Steam wishlists surpassing 2,000 and climbing. Mainstream launch, repeatedly targeted for "later this year," was eventually pinned to Q2 2025 pending world travel, crafting, and related systems. (CC1, CC99, CC102, CC107, CC118, CC120, CC122, CC124, CC128, CC129, CC130, CC131, CC132, CC134, CC137, CC140, CC141, CC144, CC145, CC146, CC147)

items.name: Steam/Epic "Coming Soon" Ad Funnels & Wishlist Goal
items.desc: active ad funnels driving traffic to the coming-soon pages, targeting a combined wishlist of 20,000--50,000 people within the year. (CC148)

items.name: Steam Version Asset Restrictions
items.desc: the Steam build is the same game, but POA/POA trading is disabled for Steam-logged-in players specifically (they can still buy via the website); reviewed and confirmed compliant against Steam's terms of service. (CC144)

items.name: Game Trailer Production (Ongoing)
items.desc: a recurring trailer-production thread feeding the Epic/Steam listings: a passport-control-style sequence through the World Breaker into the new Museum area, new cinematics leveraging UE5.5.1 movement improvements for more realistic avatar gestures, and a trailer released on YouTube ahead of storefront listing. (CC107, CC118, CC120, CC131, CC144)

items.name: Educational Section in Launcher (Original Vision)
items.desc: an onboarding/learning-resources section originally planned inside the desktop launcher itself for new players. (CC1, CC10, CC12, CC27, CC30, CC34, CC37, CC43)

items.name: Gamified Education / Badge System
items.desc: Core Concept & Evolution --- a gamified education system teaching community members about Cornucopias, crypto, and security topics; began as a Discord command-triggered quiz bot before moving to a full web app; built by a Ukraine-based dev team; specific badge categories confirmed (security, crypto onboarding, custom domes, theme zone, Copi Wiki); badges tied to Discord roles and potential future POA sale perks; eventually planned to be hosted on the same domain as the redesigned website, developed in parallel with the launcher/website foundation. (CC23, CC24, CC26, CC27, CC29, CC30, CC33, CC36)

items.name: White-Label Education Program
items.desc: a white-labeled version of the badge/education system planned for other projects to license and use for their own community education. (CC27)

items.name: Learn & Earn Platform / Copious Academy Naming
items.desc: the platform tentatively named 'Copious Academy,' where users complete quizzes on published content to earn badges (syncable to Discord, granting whitelist perks); planned to launch as an MVP and iterate from feedback. (CC37)

items.name: Copious Academy
items.desc: Development Status & Tabling --- reached roughly 90% complete (content and user-side UI remaining) before being temporarily tabled to prioritize the racing game launch; repeatedly described as launching 'shortly after the website' or 'fairly soon,' with relaunch planned before major paid marketing begins. (CC39, CC40, CC42, CC49, CC54)

items.name: Copious Academy Module (Website Integration)
items.desc: built as one of the modules within the new website's admin management console. (CC44)

items.name: Copious Academy Badge System (OG Retention Requirement)
items.desc: a plan requiring OG holders to earn and maintain a minimum number of course-based badges to retain their OG role. (CC47)

items.name: Cornucopias University Episode
items.desc: an upcoming video/AMA content episode featuring Carlos from DEGA, distinct from the Academy platform itself. (CC55)

items.name: Halloween Season (Recurring)
items.desc: the Quantum Jack pumpkin helmet was the first Halloween POA drop, with the tradition confirmed to grow each year; later builds added pumpkins, candy, a 'Horn of Plenty' cornucopia easter egg, and seasonally reskinned backpacks, plus a full Cedo Valley area transformation and Autumn/Halloween decorations added throughout the world to coincide with seasonal sales. (CC1, CC107, CC108, CC109)

items.name: Holiday/Christmas Season (Recurring)
items.desc: festive in-world decorations, seasonal POA cosmetics, and Christmas sales, confirmed as an annual tradition. (CC1, CC30)

items.name: Easter
items.desc: mentioned as a planned future seasonal event. (CC1)

items.name: District/Land Competitions (Seasonal)
items.desc: seasonal reward competitions between districts. (CC1)

items.name: Town Naming Vote
items.desc: a community vote on the 36 town names across all Solaces. (CC1)

items.name: Guild Trailer Contest
items.desc: community guilds created trailers/videos for Cornucopias; Knight's Guild won the first contest using AI-assisted production. (CC1)

items.name: Christmas POA Sale 2022 (Bobblehead, Light Kit, Racing Suit)
items.desc: a small seasonal sale bundling three items: the Farmer Joe bobblehead test mint, a vehicle light kit, and the Cheeky Crypto racing suit; the light kit sale was postponed while the racing suit sale was confirmed for December 20th. (CC30, CC33, CC34, CC35)

items.name: Monthly Content Cadence
items.desc: settled plan to deliver new content roughly once a month (new Calido sections, mine additions, new racetracks, etc.) once testing pipelines were established, targeting at least 12 releases a year plus hotfixes/specials. (CC51, CC64, CC75)

items.name: Season X
items.desc: the first major seasonal competitive event, planned for Q3/Q4, featuring racing across A/B/C/S classes with 101 winners each, plus XP-based leaderboards for gathering/crafting/raiding activities rewarding Copi; developed in parallel with land rush prep, nodes, and the racing league. (CC83, CC85)

items.name: In-Game Season Length
items.desc: four in-game seasons planned per year, roughly 12-13 human weeks each, once the game is fully live. (CC85)

items.name: Seasonal Progression System
items.desc: four 13-week seasons per year with seasonal resets, in-season leveling, and seasonal competitions culminating in a final week; reaching top level yields a season-exclusive POA reward. (CC97)

items.name: Quantum Autumn Sale & Build
items.desc: a named sale/build launching around Oct 23rd with rotating Cardano/Base assets, nearly all usable immediately in the next build (except the cargo ship); delayed by a DoS attack and configuration issues before ultimately running for 21 days. (CC108, CC109)

items.name: Glimpse of Fear
items.desc: a new seasonal area replacing the outdated Glimpse of Solace. (CC110)

items.name: Glimpse of Esperanza
items.desc: a follow-up seasonal area planned for a different location than the prior Glimpse of Solace/Fear. (CC110)

items.name: Avatar Creator / Avatar 3.0 Contest
items.desc: a cross-community contest (Superverse and Medicaid confirmed, Neotokyo/Lizard Labs pending) giving away $10,000 worth of Copi, timed alongside the phase-3 weapon sale and leading into the land grab and apartment sale. (CC130, CC132, CC134, CC137)

items.name: Holiday Cosmetic Items (Quanti the Snowman, Festive Gear)
items.desc: limited-edition holiday items in the Cyber Monday sale: apartment decorations, festive hats/backpacks, and a dark/corrupted 'Quanti the Snowman' variant of the Quantum Jack helmet line. (CC145)

items.name: Very Mythical Christmas Sale
items.desc: a holiday thank-you sale (originally planned as Cyber Monday) for existing community members, offering reduced-quantity cosmetic/vehicle assets, running ~3 weeks or until sold out. (CC146)

items.name: Dirt Birds Raffle (OG Legendary Sprinter)
items.desc: a joint raffle at the cNFTcon booth that sold 10,000+ tickets, with Discord user VJ420 selected as the winner live at the event. (CC26)

items.name: 2023 'Year of the Corn' Meme Contest
items.desc: a community meme contest with an POA prize for the winner. (CC36)

items.name: Twitter Meme Contest & Anniversary Giveaways
items.desc: a moonshot/rocket-themed meme contest with POA prizes, plus additional contests/giveaways tied to the Copi Cafe one-year anniversary (March 26th). (CC47)

items.name: File Nodes
items.desc: Core Concept --- already live, handling game data distribution to reduce AWS server costs; node rewards pay Copi to operators over time; cross-chain node sales confirmed live on both Ethereum and Cardano. (CC1)

items.name: Decentralized File Distribution
items.desc: Prototype to Commercial Software --- a working prototype cut game download times from 45+ minutes to 5-7 minutes by pulling files in parallel from player-run nodes (a torrent-like CDN); custom software (not off-the-shelf BitTorrent) was written in-house, evolving from proof-of-concept to commercial-grade, eventually supporting Windows, Linux, Mac, and Raspberry Pi; a single PC was proven able to run up to 100 node licenses at once. (CC69, CC72, CC73, CC74, CC92, CC94, CC109, CC112, CC115)

items.name: Node Sale
items.desc: Multi-Year Timeline (Cardano, Base, Ethereum) --- sales rolled out in tiers across three chains over roughly two years: Cardano tiers 1A/1B through 5 sold progressively (1,000+ nodes per early tier, ~100 sold within 24 hours at tier 5), an Ethereum Layer-2 sale launched as the first cross-chain POA effort, and a further ETH sale opened on Base (via USDT/MetaMask); combined totals passed 4,500 on Cardano and 1,800+ on Base at one point, climbing toward a final total of roughly 9,000 nodes; sales paused periodically to let the team catch up on delivery/software before reopening. (CC74, CC75, CC76, CC77, CC78, CC80, CC81, CC82, CC83, CC84, CC86, CC89, CC95, CC98, CC99, CC147)

items.name: Custom Game Launcher (Node-Integrated)
items.desc: Cornucopias built its own proprietary launcher rather than relying on third-party platforms, tightly integrated with node infrastructure. (CC75)

items.name: Node Software Hosting Options (Home PC, VPS, Raspberry Pi)
items.desc: commercial node software confirmed running across Windows, Linux, Mac, and Raspberry Pi (sub-$200 hardware, with one Pi becoming a top performer in testing); VPS hosting confirmed as a viable path for non-technical operators, with a partner-built VPS service explored alongside home-hardware options. (CC77, CC94, CC97, CC107, CC109, CC112)

items.name: Public Node Pools & Delegation System
items.desc: a delegation system letting node owners point to a public pool with zero extra setup, or open their own public pool (minimum owned-node requirement eventually lowered from 8 to 6, cap of 15,000 Copi/COPI per pool); delegate caps per node doubled from 2 to 4; a front-end management interface (pool naming, online/offline/syncing status, API keys, logs) was built out; by CC135, ~150 public pools existed with ~4,966 delegates and 3,271 nodes still undelegated. (CC91, CC92, CC94, CC97, CC111, CC112, CC114, CC126, CC133, CC135, CC146, CC149)

items.name: Node Reward Structure
items.desc: Base vs. Performance Split (Evolving) --- rewards began fully even across all registered nodes, then shifted gradually toward performance-based payouts: 99%/1% base/performance, later 75%/25% (from Sept 1), then targeting 10%/90% base/performance by the following year; delegation enforcement eventually cut rewards for inactive/non-delegating license holders to activate dormant nodes. First-year DePIN rewards were set at 26 million COPI distributed to active node holders. (CC93, CC119, CC125, CC131, CC132, CC135, CC139)

items.name: Node Reward Claiming, Dashboards & Calculators
items.desc: a public rewards dashboard (audited smart contract on Base, Drip Drop partnership for Cardano) let operators view (then later claim) earned rewards, gated by KYC above $500/day; a companion rewards calculator (prototyped with ChatGPT-4o, then built out fully) let anyone estimate daily/annual rewards from nodes sold, participation rate, and delegate setup; separate performance-monitoring dashboards tracked pool 'strength' (check-ins, request success rate, delegation counts/speed) with region/availability filters. (CC94, CC95, CC105, CC106, CC107, CC109, CC112, CC122, CC123, CC124, CC125)

items.name: Node-Based Game Download System
items.desc: Rollout to Full Production --- nodes progressively took over serving the actual game download/update files from AWS: internal testing cut per-download hosting cost from ~$2.70-3 (and later from ~£3,000 per build release down to ~$90, a ~95% reduction); local node detection, direct-from-node download utilities, and full launcher integration followed; a live mass community test (watch-party download event) succeeded despite some routing issues; culminating in a build where every download was served entirely through node infrastructure rather than AWS, working well overall with some regional bottlenecks. (CC102, CC103, CC104, CC106, CC107, CC108, CC109, CC117, CC118, CC119, CC120, CC122, CC126, CC132)

items.name: Node Community Testing Events
items.desc: 'Breaking Corn' Stress Tests --- scheduled community stress-test events where testers gradually increased concurrent players (or mass-triggered simultaneous redownloads) to find server breaking points; the first event (100+ participants) surfaced rubber-banding from mismatched regional servers, feeding API and region-matching improvements. (CC73, CC74, CC119)

items.name: Node Operator Testing, Documentation & Community Engagement
items.desc: early invited testing groups (15-20 then 20-person groups) onboarded via dedicated Discord channels; setup documentation/videos covered Windows/Mac/Linux/Docker installation; regular operator-specific communications and a dedicated Node Operator Summit (roadmap presentation, Q&A, new node-type previews) were organized separately from general community AMAs. (CC79, CC102, CC106, CC109, CC111, CC131, CC136, CC147, CC148, CC149)

items.name: Server Nodes (New Node Type, Custom Domes)
items.desc: a planned second node type beyond file nodes, letting community members host multiplayer Custom Dome servers, paid in RISE token; ~50 free test server nodes planned for existing high-capacity file node operators; proper development targeted to start in January, with long-term ambitions of hosting Cornucopias' own infrastructure on community server nodes; explicitly noted as not guaranteed to launch. (CC1, CC146, CC147, CC149, CC151)

items.name: Decentralized Server Infrastructure (Long-Term Goal)
items.desc: a long-term ambition to reduce reliance on Amazon AWS overall, beyond just file distribution. (CC1)

items.name: Esperanza Server Repurposing
items.desc: underused/low-traffic Europe servers repurposed for Esperanza development work, with active players shifted to US servers. (CC1, CC151)

items.name: Node + Launcher Integration (Automatic Detection)
items.desc: the desktop launcher automatically detects and manages nodes, applied later to secondary marketplace integration work as well. (CC1, CC10, CC12, CC34, CC37, CC43, CC152)

items.name: Role-Based Access & Permission Systems
items.desc: systems letting the team grant/restrict access to specific game features or areas in real time via a web portal (e.g. POA rarity tier gating, opening/closing broken zones like the observation tower), used throughout staged testing rollouts; granular per-testing-group toggles confirmed live. (CC51, CC57, CC60)

items.name: Server Scaling Architecture
items.desc: Custom-Built vs. GameLift --- the team evaluated and ultimately moved away from Amazon GameLift for core server/matchmaking architecture (citing game scale), building custom session/matchmaking infrastructure in-house instead; AWS auto-scaling was later built to spin up individual game sessions (Solace, Pavilion, race tracks) independently, supporting hundreds of thousands of players; GameLift/EC2 was still used in earlier testing phases (multi-region EU/US servers, 6-player 4K60fps replication tests) before the custom system matured. (CC40, CC50, CC52, CC61, CC63, CC64, CC76, CC77, CC85, CC98, CC117, CC119, CC127)

items.name: Multi-Region & Latency Infrastructure
items.desc: 24-hour AWS-hosted EU and US test servers made selectable from the main menu; geographic player grouping and regional server expansion (Asia/Australia requested via survey) pursued to reduce latency; a tiered regional node-pool network (Chicago/Amsterdam hubs feeding dozens of regional pools, expanding toward Singapore, Puerto Rico/Costa Rica, and Australia) built a global demand heat map for reward balancing. (CC40, CC61, CC77, CC112, CC120, CC144)

items.name: Build & Deployment Pipeline
items.desc: CI/CD Automation --- cloud-based automatic code compilation after GitHub pushes (freeing developer PCs from hours-long local builds), Linux cross-compilation for backend servers (cutting hosting costs up to 50%), blue-green deployment for managing live vs. new builds, and a fully automated build pipeline (with Discord build-complete notifications) eliminating manual release work. (CC61, CC63, CC95)

items.name: Backend Data & Security Migration (Server-Side Authority)
items.desc: client-side game logic (avatar settings, race times, holo caches, inventory) progressively moved to server-side/database processing (DynamoDB, the same tech behind Amazon's New World MMO) to prevent client-side hacking/tampering; player-replicated data was later compressed for a 50% reduction in bandwidth per player. (CC83, CC85, CC87, CC99, CC146)

items.name: Security & Blockchain Audits
items.desc: planned security audits across all in-game endpoints plus a separate blockchain/web3 audit before real asset value was at stake, to prevent exploits and protect funds. (CC62)

items.name: Testnet Economy, Security Bounty & Multisig
items.desc: the full in-game economy (POA minting, test-coin trading) built and tested on Cardano testnet before mainnet migration; a community security bounty incentivized players and experienced Cardano developers to try to break the system; multisig and other best-practice authentication measures protected the treasury throughout. (CC5)

items.name: API Authentication & Security (Play-to-Earn Prep)
items.desc: roughly six months spent building secure APIs for authentication and token exchange across Android/Apple/PC, specifically to prevent hacking before enabling play-to-earn features. (CC14)

items.name: Cross-Chain Bridges
items.desc: ChainPort, Milkomeda & Timeport --- the BSC-to-Cardano bridge partnership with ChainPort (IOHK dev-environment support, independent auditing) moved through a lengthy audit/QA process before launch; a separate centralized bridge tied to the Milkomeda hard fork (95% of tokens held off-site, Certik-audited, IOHK-involved) went live; and the 'Timeport' bridge infrastructure launched on Halloween (Oct 31, 2022), described at the time as a major ecosystem milestone. (CC12, CC16, CC28, CC29, CC36)

items.name: Cornucopias Cardano Stake Pool (Infrastructure Note)
items.desc: launched August 3, 2022, growing to ~50M ADA staked and producing 1,100+ blocks as a single non-ISPO pool supporting Cardano network decentralization. (CC36)

items.name: Unreal Engine Version Upgrades
items.desc: the project moved through successive UE5 versions (5.3 → 5.5 → 5.5.4) to fix technical/material issues and unlock new features; UE5.5 specifically brought Mega Lighting, reducing the ~200 manually placed lights needed in Calido City for realistic bounce lighting. (CC116, CC128)

items.name: FSR (AMD Upscaling) Support
items.desc: AMD's FidelityFX Super Resolution added as a companion to the already-released Nvidia DLSS, improving performance across a broader range of graphics cards. (CC140)

items.name: Hardware Requirement Adjustments
items.desc: minimum VRAM requirement raised to 6GB during testing (lower-end 10-series cards not yet tuned), later followed by removing GPU restrictions entirely so lower-end cards could rejoin once optimizations landed. (CC62, CC101)

items.name: QA & Bug Tracking Pipeline
items.desc: a three-tier support pipeline (Freshdesk intake → Jira escalation → developer resolution) handled roughly 800 tester-reported bugs at one point, triaged by severity; GPS-coordinate auto-capture on tester screenshots and automatic system-spec logging aided debugging; testing processes were later expanded to larger groups with more statistical QA signal-gathering. (CC15, CC48, CC56, CC63, CC133)

items.name: Database & API Infrastructure (XP, Progression, Racing/POA Data)
items.desc: a hire dedicated to building secure database/API systems for XP, progression, and item data; a Layer-2 partnership with DEGA/DGA to store racing vehicle and player race history off Cardano Layer 1 (reducing transaction costs, enabling third-party API access) with dynamic POAs planned as a future extension; cloud saving added for race times. (CC53, CC57, CC66, CC70, CC87)

items.name: Cornucopias Labs Testing Platform (North Point Hills)
items.desc: a compartmentalized virtual testing environment for mining, plot building, resource gathering, and farming (eventually PvP), isolated from the live game world for safe testing. (CC66)

items.name: In-Game Asset Usability API
items.desc: backend modifications letting newly purchased POA items be read and used immediately in-game upon purchase. (CC105)

items.name: Sector/Property Performance Testing
items.desc: testing how many properties a sector could support performantly; original plan (4 districts × 200 properties = 800/sector) revised based on real performance data and UE5.1 gains. (CC32)

items.name: 3D Grid System for Solace Development
items.desc: a sector-grid overlay (e.g. A3, A4) letting the team assign developers/testers to specific map areas, aiding bug tracking at the scale of an 8km×8km map. (CC36)

items.name: Minting Queue & War Room Infrastructure
items.desc: live sale dashboards, a global 'war room' team, database queueing for tens of thousands of concurrent users, and email/browser fail-safes, built to manage high-traffic POA mint events. (CC9)

items.name: POA Website Access-Restriction Tech
items.desc: proprietary tech restricting/managing concurrent visitors to the land sale website to control mint-time traffic. (CC6)

items.name: Website Central Admin / Backend Infrastructure
items.desc: a central admin system behind the redesigned website supporting future modules (POA/rewards dashboard, Academy-style content). (CC41)

items.name: Nav Mesh Performance Optimization
items.desc: active performance testing of the navigation mesh due to issues from the large scale of the Calypso zone. (CC153)

items.name: Solace Apartment Persistence Infrastructure
items.desc: backend technology supporting 50,000 individual persistent apartments in Solace, shared and synced across all servers. (CC156)

items.name: Host-to-Earn Nodes (Early Roadmap Mention)
items.desc: two types of host-to-earn nodes referenced as part of the active roadmap, with further Wiki explanation planned. (CC3)

items.name: Data Domes/Nodes Research (Delayed)
items.desc: early-stage 'data domes/nodes' research pushed to Q4 pending further investigation. (CC12)

items.name: Nodes Feature (Early Delay, Grouped With Pets/Mounts)
items.desc: the nodes roadmap item delayed alongside pets and mounts, without further specifics given at the time. (CC17)

items.name: Elevator Speed & General Hotfixes
items.desc: a hotfix increasing elevator speed (previously slow for penthouse-floor apartments) alongside several other bug fixes. (CC155)

items.name: Full Lore Bible
items.desc: Core Vision & Rollout Plan --- a full origin story planned and written in outline form (~50 lore shots), developed by a dedicated writing team (plus Rob and Josh) over about nine months; revealed gradually through cinematics built using existing game art/programming (no resource diversion needed), each paired with accompanying literature, with the complete story eventually posted to the Wiki and other unannounced mediums; designed to evolve over 2-4 years tied to game seasons, strong enough to stand alone as a cinematic or movie short. (CC1, CC21, CC45, CC49, CC55)

items.name: Storyline: The Mars Stargate
items.desc: humanity discovers a Stargate on Mars, leading to the founding of Cornucopias. (CC1)

items.name: The Multiverse & World Gates
items.desc: Cornucopias exists within a multiverse; multiple versions of Earth exist, each with at least one World Gate. (CC1)

items.name: The World Gate
items.desc: the very first gate ever built, predating the Cloud Gate, which enabled original multiverse travel between Earths; central to the origin of the Calamity and the rift threat; concept art exists and may feature in the game trailer. (CC1)

items.name: The 12 Architects
items.desc: the beings who created Cornucopias, central to its founding mythology ('Cornucopias is our salvation, we owe them a debt that can never be paid'). (CC1)

items.name: The Terra
items.desc: Enemy Faction --- an intelligent, organized enemy faction ('The Terra hate us because we are chosen'), distinct from Quantum Monsters, revealed later as people left behind on Earth after humanity's ascension; deep lore developed with their full story still to unfold. (CC1, CC103)

items.name: The Outlaws / Gunslingers
items.desc: Scrapped, Folded Into The Terra --- an early-concept rival faction tied to Wild West zone lore, raiding corn trains to steal biofuel for a cheaper competing fuel source; this concept was pivoted into The Terra and related factions. (CC2)

items.name: The Calamity
items.desc: the catastrophic event that drove humanity from Earth's surface to the sky, directly connected to the World Gate and The Terra. (CC1)

items.name: The World Breaker
items.desc: the ship/structure players start the game in, representing in-lore how players travel from Earth to Cornucopias; robot T-355 welcomes players aboard. (CC1)

items.name: Rando's Metal Works / Junkers
items.desc: Randy, a surface-dweller who built useful technology from scrap and junk, created the 'Junkers' aesthetic line of vehicles, weapons, and items. (CC1)

items.name: The Rift Threat
items.desc: an unrevealed force controlling and sending creatures through rifts, with the mystery meant to unfold gradually over time. (CC1)

items.name: Alleian Ship / New Player Arrival Sequence
items.desc: new players learn the lore through an onboarding ship sequence, flying in and landing to represent their journey from Earth into Cornucopias; a full, polished version of this sequence exists but was disabled/reserved for a more public release stage past testing. (CC1, CC66)

items.name: NPC Characters With Full Names & Backstories
items.desc: named characters in active development including Carl, Abigail, and Farmer Joe (Old Guard, defends the corn train in the Wild West zone). (CC1, CC2)

items.name: World History Integrated Into Environment
items.desc: lore woven into posters, terminals, and NPC dialogue throughout the world. (CC1)

items.name: Crash Site Lore & Relic Quest
items.desc: ships crash-landed in Solis scattering ancient relics, tying into the Relic Quest; later realized via a Maxwell Caldera cinematic introducing crash-site relic hunting across the Solaces, with relics (worth up to 100k+ IGC) sellable at the antique shop and respawn timers tuned by rarity. (CC1, CC155)

items.name: Quantum Monsters & Lore Portals in Mines
items.desc: mines confirmed to feature lore elements including portals and Quantum Monsters tied into the mining loop; later expanded via 'Julia's Story,' a Quantum Monster-tied narrative included with the Glimpse of Fear update. (CC65, CC109)

items.name: Origin Story
items.desc: Release Delays --- origin story content largely ready but delayed multiple times for proper cinematic/animation treatment; originally planned for January 2023, still pending as of this mention. (CC74)

items.name: Expanded Game Lore & World/Story Detail
items.desc: ongoing work with the team's dedicated writer to incorporate more lore into the game as part of the year's content push, adding detail to established world/story lore and finalizing release timing for new content. (CC81, CC86, CC101)

items.name: Lore Acceleration Initiative (Marketing)
items.desc: a marketing push to accelerate lore release through fun, interactive mediums intended to build player attachment, hype, and shareable content. (CC83)

items.name: Concept Art Book
items.desc: a 50+ page book by David featuring Solace, Esperanza, and creatures (Quantum Bears, foxes, wolves), revealed in pages over several weeks with some potentially minted as POAs. (CC101)

items.name: Game Trailer / Lore Video (Earth, Calamity, Architects)
items.desc: a cinematic trailer (~50 shots) covering core lore beats, with an estimated 6-week production build. (CC102)

items.name: Museum (Lore Hub)
items.desc: a starting-experience area showcasing world technology, the first Gen Core, the Cradle where Genesian was synthesized, and a Bubble Jet Prima display, doubling as content for the Epic Games Store trailer. (CC120)

items.name: Game Cinematic Production (Motion Matching/Mocap)
items.desc: a cinematic in production using motion matching and mocap suit technology to capture actual in-game-quality graphics rather than pre-rendered visuals, extending production time as new tech became available. (CC122)

items.name: Globe / Calamity Visualization (Alleian)
items.desc: a projected globe inside the Alleian showing Earth's altered geography and ongoing quantum calamity activity (ocean shifts, tectonic changes), highlighting Kilo Valley and Cornucopias locations relative to the World Gate and Atlantic Ridge. (CC129)

items.name: Rebrand to Infinity Rising
